sk: तपसा चीयते ब्रह्म ततोऽन्नमभिजायते अन्नात्प्राणो मनः सत्यं लोकाः कर्मसु चामृतम् ||
ro: tapasā · cīyate · brahma · tataḥ · annam · abhijāyate · annāt · prāṇaḥ · manaḥ · satyaṁ · lokāḥ · karmasu · ca · amṛtam ||
hi: तपसा (by tapas / तप से) ब्रह्म (Brahman) चीयते (is built up / संचित होता है)। ततः (from that) अन्नम् (food / matter) अभिजायते (is born)। अन्न से प्राण (life-breath), मनः (mind), सत्यम् (truth), लोकाः (worlds), और कर्मसु अमृतम् (in actions, immortality) [उत्पन्न होते हैं]।
en: By tapas (austerity), Brahman is built up (cīyate); from that, food/matter (anna) is born. From food [come] prāṇa, manas (mind), truth (satya), the worlds (lokāḥ), and immortality in actions (karmasu amṛtam).

ws.h: संचित होता है / निर्मित होता है
ws.e: is built up / is piled up

ws.h: उत्पन्न होता है / जन्म लेता है

gr:
व्याकरण: तपसा — 'तपस्' (तप) का तृतीया एकवचन (instrumental singular) — 'तप के द्वारा।' चीयते — √चि (संचय करना / राशि बनाना) कर्मणि वर्तमान (passive present) — 'संचित होता है / निर्मित किया जाता है' — मूलतः वैदिक अग्नि-चयन (fire-altar building) का शब्द — यहाँ रूपक: ब्रह्म का 'निर्माण' तप से। ततः = 'उससे' — पञ्चमी अर्थ में अव्यय। अन्नम् अभिजायते — 'अन्नम्' = अन्न/पदार्थ; 'अभिजायते' = अभि + √जन् — 'प्रकट रूप से उत्पन्न होता है।' अन्नात् — पञ्चमी (ablative) — 'अन्न से।' प्राणः मनः सत्यम् — सृष्टि-क्रम: अन्न → प्राण → मनस् → सत्यम् — स्थूल से सूक्ष्म की ओर। लोकाः — प्रथमा बहुवचन — 'लोक / भुवन।' कर्मसु अमृतम् — 'कर्मसु' = सप्तमी बहुवचन (locative plural) — 'कर्मों में'; 'अमृतम्' = अ + मृत — 'मृत्यु-रहित / अमर' — कर्म-क्षेत्र में अमरत्व — ज्ञानी के कर्म बन्धनकारी नहीं। यह मन्त्र मुण्डक में तृतीय बार (2.2.10, 3.1.5, 3.2.1) आता है — त्रिपुनरुक्ति = परम बल — मौखिक परम्परा में सर्वोच्च स्मृति-अंकन।
Eng: 'Tapasā' = instrumental of tapas. 'Cīyate' = passive of √ci (to pile up) — originally the Vedic fire-altar building term, here metaphorical. The creation sequence: tapas → brahma → anna → prāṇa → manas → satya → lokāḥ → karmasu amṛtam. Triple repetition (2.2.10, 3.1.5, 3.2.1) = supreme emphasis in oral tradition.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — तीसरी बार पुनरुक्ति (third repetition) = अत्यन्त बल (utmost emphasis)। 'तपसा चीयते ब्रह्म' = ज्ञान-तप (knowledge-tapas) से ब्रह्म-साक्षात्कार (Brahman-realisation) संचित (accumulated) होता है। यह मन्त्र पूरे उपनिषद् का मेरुदण्ड (backbone) है।
advaita.en: Shankara says third repetition = utmost emphasis. 'Tapasā cīyate brahma' = through knowledge-tapas, Brahman-realisation is accumulated. This mantra is the backbone of the entire Upanishad.
advaita.ins: Said once — a teaching. Said twice — a reminder. Said three times — a truth the Upanishad wants you to carry forever. Build up Brahman within yourself through tapas. Everything flows from that — life, mind, truth, worlds, and the deathless spark in every action.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — तृतीय पुनरुक्ति = भगवद्-ज्ञान (God-knowledge) और भक्ति-तप (devotion-tapas) का सर्वोच्च बल। यह मन्त्र अन्तिम खण्ड (final section) का द्वार खोलता है — जहाँ सत्य (truth) और भगवत्-प्राप्ति (God-attainment) का वर्णन होगा।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says third repetition = supreme emphasis on God-knowledge and devotion-tapas. This mantra opens the final section — where truth and God-attainment will be described.
vishisht.ins: Three times the Upanishad tells you: build up God-knowledge through devotion. Because it's opening the final door now — the door to truth itself, to the path that leads to God. Listen carefully to what follows.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — तीन बार = चेतना-शक्ति (consciousness-force / tapas) की त्रि-स्तरीय कार्यप्रणाली: (1) सृष्टि (creation — Muṇḍaka 2), (2) अभ्यास (practice — 3.1), (3) सत्य-प्राप्ति (truth-attainment — 3.2)। एक ही शक्ति — तीन अनुप्रयोग (applications)।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says three repetitions = the triple operation of consciousness-force (tapas): (1) creation (Muṇḍaka 2), (2) practice (3.1), (3) truth-attainment (3.2). One force — three applications.
aurobindo.ins: The same consciousness-force works at every level. It creates the universe. It builds your practice. And now — it opens the door to truth. Three times the mantra appears because consciousness operates at three scales — cosmic, personal, and ultimate.

dp.q: 🔍 The triple repetition — architecture of the Muṇḍaka
dp.a:
इस मन्त्र की तीन बार पुनरुक्ति (2.2.10, 3.1.5, 3.2.1) मुण्डक उपनिषद् का संरचनात्मक ढाँचा बनाती है। प्रथम प्रकटन (2.2.10): ध्यान-शिक्षा के अन्त में — प्रणव-धनुष, आत्मा-बाण, ब्रह्म-लक्ष्य ध्यान के पश्चात् — अनुप्रयोग: सृष्टिविज्ञानपरक (cosmological)। द्वितीय प्रकटन (3.1.5): दो पक्षियों के प्रसंग में — अनुप्रयोग: व्यक्तिगत/मोक्षपरक। तृतीय प्रकटन (3.2.1): अन्तिम खण्ड का द्वार — 'सत्यमेव जयते' की ओर — अनुप्रयोग: चरमोत्कर्ष। क्रम: सृष्टिपरक → व्यक्तिपरक → चरम। वही तप जो सृष्टि रचता है — साधक का अभ्यास बनता है — और अन्तिम सत्य प्रकट करता है। मौखिक परम्परा में त्रिपुनरुक्ति सर्वाधिक शक्तिशाली स्मृति-अंकन था — 'जो तीन बार कहा जाए वह सत्य हो जाता है।'

Eng: This mantra's three appearances (2.2.10, 3.1.5, 3.2.1) form the structural skeleton of the Muṇḍaka's second half: First appearance (2.2.10): at the end of the meditation teachings. Context: after the bow-and-arrow meditation (praṇava = bow, ātmā = arrow, brahma = target) and the OM-meditation. Meaning: Brahman's tapas is the creative force — it produces everything from food to immortality. Application: cosmological. Second appearance (3.1.5): at the heart of the two-birds section. Context: between the parable of the two birds (3.1.1-4) and the bridge-verses (3.1.5-7). Meaning: the aspirant's tapas builds up Brahman-knowledge within. Application: personal/soteriological. Third appearance (3.2.1): at the opening of the final Khanda — the 'Satyameva Jayate' section. Context: the verse now stands as a gateway to the Upanishad's climactic teachings on truth, the path, and final liberation. Application: culminating/eschatological. The pattern: cosmological → personal → ultimate. The same tapas that creates the world empowers the individual and reveals the final truth. In oral tradition: triple repetition was the strongest mnemonic device — what is said three times becomes indelibly imprinted on the student's memory.

dp.q: 🔍 'Karmasu amṛtam' — immortality within action
dp.a:
'कर्मसु अमृतम्' (कर्मों में अमरत्व) मुण्डक की एक प्रमुख शिक्षा को समाहित करता है — शाश्वत को क्षणिक में खोजना। विरोधाभास: कर्म (action) स्वभावतः सीमित — आदि, मध्य, अन्त। तो अमृत (अमरत्व) कर्मों 'में' कैसे? समाधान: जब कर्म ब्रह्म-ज्ञान से अनुप्राणित हों, तो वे साधारण कर्म नहीं रहते — शाश्वत की अभिव्यक्ति बन जाते हैं। ज्ञानी आत्मक्रीड़ और आत्मरति (3.1.4) से कर्म करता है — ऐसा कर्म बन्धनकारी नहीं, मुक्तिकारी। तीन स्तर: (1) कर्मकाण्डीय: सम्यक् यज्ञ = स्वर्ग-लोक। (2) नैतिक: सत्य-आधारित कर्म = ऋत (विश्व-व्यवस्था) में सहभागिता। (3) आध्यात्मिक: ब्रह्मज्ञानी का कर्म = अमृत — क्योंकि अक्षर आत्मा से उत्पन्न, अक्षर में विलीन — कोई कर्म-बन्धन नहीं। गीता (4.24): 'ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्म हविः ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम्' — जब सब ब्रह्म, तो हर कर्म अमृत।

Eng: The phrase 'karmasu amṛtam' (immortality in actions) encapsulates a key Muṇḍaka teaching — that the eternal can be found within the temporal: The paradox: karma (action) is, by definition, finite — it has a beginning, a middle, and an end. How can amṛta (immortality/deathlessness) exist 'in' actions? The resolution: when actions are informed by Brahman-knowledge (tapas → brahma), they cease to be ordinary karma. They become expressions of the eternal within the temporal. The knower acts from Self-delight (ātma-krīḍa, ātma-rati — 3.1.4), and such action is not binding but liberating. Three levels of understanding: (1) Ritualistic: the Vedic rituals, when performed correctly, yield imperishable results — the 'immortality' of heavenly worlds. (2) Ethical: actions rooted in truth (satya) have an imperishable dimension — they participate in the cosmic order (ṛta). (3) Spiritual: the Brahman-knower's actions are amṛta because they arise from and return to the imperishable Self — there is no karma created, no bondage generated, no saṁsāra perpetuated. The Gītā's elaboration (4.24): 'brahmārpaṇaṁ brahma haviḥ brahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam' — 'the offering is Brahman, the oblation is Brahman, poured by Brahman into the fire of Brahman.' When everything is Brahman, every action is immortal.

sk: यः सर्वज्ञः सर्ववित्यस्य ज्ञानमयं तपः तस्मादेतद्ब्रह्म नाम रूपमन्नं च जायते ||
ro: yaḥ · sarva-jñaḥ · sarva-vit · yasya · jñāna-mayaṁ · tapaḥ · tasmāt · etat · brahma · nāma · rūpam · annaṁ · ca · jāyate ||
hi: जो (यः) सर्वज्ञ (omniscient) है, सर्ववित् (all-knowing) है, जिसका (यस्य) तप (tapas) ज्ञानमय (made of knowledge / ज्ञान-स्वरूप) है — उससे (तस्मात्) यह ब्रह्म (Vedic creative principle), नाम (name), रूप (form), और अन्न (food/matter) जायते (is born)।
en: He who is omniscient (sarva-jña), all-knowing (sarva-vit), whose tapas (tapaḥ) is made of knowledge (jñāna-mayam) — from Him are born this Brahman, name (nāma), form (rūpa), and food (anna).

ws.e: made of knowledge / consisting of knowledge

ws.h: उत्पन्न होता है / जन्म लेता है

gr:
व्याकरण: यः — सर्वनाम, प्रथमा एकवचन — 'जो / वह जो।' सर्वज्ञः — सर्व (सब) + ज्ञ (√ज्ञा = जानना) — बहुव्रीहि — 'जो सब जानता है।' सर्ववित् — सर्व + विद् (√विद् = जानना) — 'सर्ववेत्ता' — सर्वज्ञ और सर्ववित् में सूक्ष्म भेद: सर्वज्ञ = सामान्य ज्ञान (general knowledge), सर्ववित् = विशेष ज्ञान (particular knowledge of each thing)। यस्य — षष्ठी एकवचन — 'जिसका।' ज्ञानमयम् — ज्ञान + मयट् प्रत्यय — 'ज्ञान-स्वरूप / ज्ञान से परिपूर्ण' — ब्रह्म का तप अन्ध ऊर्जा नहीं, शुद्ध ज्ञान। तपः — √तप् (तपना) — प्रथमा एकवचन। तस्मात् — पञ्चमी (ablative) — 'उससे।' नाम रूपम् — द्वन्द्व समास — 'नाम और रूप' — सम्पूर्ण दृश्य जगत् = नाम-रूप। जायते — √जन् (उत्पन्न होना) आत्मनेपद वर्तमान — 'उत्पन्न होता है।' यह मन्त्र वलय-रचना (ring composition) बनाता है — 'ज्ञानमयं तपः' का पद 1.1.9 में सर्वप्रथम और 3.2.2 में अन्तिम बार — उपनिषद् का आरम्भ और समापन एक ही पद से।
Eng: 'Sarva-jñaḥ' (sarva + √jñā) = omniscient (general knowledge); 'sarva-vit' (sarva + √vid) = all-knowing (particular knowledge). 'Jñāna-mayam' = mayaṭ suffix on jñāna — 'constituted of knowledge.' 'Nāma rūpam' = dvandva compound — the phenomenal world. This verse forms a ring-composition: 'jñāna-mayaṁ tapaḥ' first appears at 1.1.9 and returns here at 3.2.2.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — 'ज्ञानमयं तपः' = ब्रह्म का तप = शुद्ध ज्ञान (pure knowledge) — अन्ध ऊर्जा (blind energy) नहीं। 'नाम-रूप' = संसार = मिथ्या (illusory appearance) — ब्रह्म पर अध्यारोपित (superimposed on Brahman)। ब्रह्म = अधिष्ठान (substratum) — नाम-रूप = आभास (appearance)।
advaita.en: Shankara says 'jñāna-mayaṁ tapaḥ' = Brahman's tapas = pure knowledge — not blind energy. 'Nāma-rūpa' = the world = illusory appearance — superimposed on Brahman. Brahman = the substratum — nāma-rūpa = the appearance.
advaita.ins: Brahman's creative power isn't blind force — it's pure intelligence. From that intelligence arise all names and forms — everything you see, hear, touch. But names and forms are not Brahman itself — they're appearances on the unchanging screen of consciousness. Know the screen, and the movie can't deceive you.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — 'ज्ञानमयं तपः' = भगवान् का तप = सर्वज्ञ संकल्प (omniscient will)। 'नाम-रूप' = सृष्टि = भगवान् का वास्तविक विकास (real transformation) — मिथ्या (illusion) नहीं। सृष्टि = भगवान् का शरीर (body of God)।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says 'jñāna-mayaṁ tapaḥ' = the Lord's tapas = omniscient will. 'Nāma-rūpa' = creation = the Lord's real transformation — not illusion. Creation = the body of God.
vishisht.ins: God creates with omniscient will — knowing everything that will emerge. Names and forms aren't illusions — they're God's real self-expression. The world is His body, and every named, formed thing is a real part of Him.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — 'ज्ञानमयं तपः' = सत्य-चेतना (truth-consciousness) — सच्चिदानन्द (sat-cit-ānanda) की सृजनात्मक शक्ति। 'नाम-रूप' = चेतना का विभेदन (differentiation of consciousness) — अवरोहण (involution) की प्रक्रिया — जिससे जड़ पदार्थ (matter / anna) तक पहुँचती है।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says 'jñāna-mayaṁ tapaḥ' = truth-consciousness — the creative power of sat-cit-ānanda. 'Nāma-rūpa' = the differentiation of consciousness — the process of involution — through which consciousness descends even to matter (anna).
aurobindo.ins: Consciousness creates through knowledge, not force. It differentiates itself into names and forms — not losing itself but expressing itself. From pure awareness to matter, every level is consciousness in a different mode. The tapas that creates is truth-consciousness, and everything it creates carries that truth within.

dp.q: 🔍 'Jñāna-mayaṁ tapaḥ' — the ring-composition of the Muṇḍaka
dp.a:
'ज्ञानमयं तपः' (ज्ञान-स्वरूप तप) पूरे मुण्डक उपनिषद् में एक वलय-रचना (ring composition) निर्मित करता है। प्रथम प्रकटन (1.1.9): शिक्षा के आरम्भ में — 'यः सर्वज्ञः सर्ववित् यस्य ज्ञानमयं तपः' — उद्घाटन-घोषणा। अन्तिम प्रकटन (3.2.2): उपनिषद् के समापन-भाग में — वही पद लौटता है — वृत्त पूर्ण। बीच में जो कुछ पढ़ाया (दो प्रकार के ज्ञान, अग्नि-विद्या, धनुष-ध्यान, दो पक्षी, नदी-समुद्र उपमा, 'ब्रह्मविद् ब्रह्मैव भवति') — सब इस वृत्त के भीतर। 'ज्ञानमय तप' का अर्थ: (1) ब्रह्म की सृजन-शक्ति बुद्धिमान है — यान्त्रिक नहीं — तप का सार ज्ञान (knowledge) है। (2) यह भौतिकवाद (जड़ पदार्थ से सृष्टि) और स्वेच्छावाद (मनमाने संकल्प से सृष्टि) दोनों से भिन्न। (3) साधक का तप भी 'ज्ञानमय' होना चाहिए — केवल शारीरिक तपस्या नहीं, ज्ञान-संपृक्त।

Eng: The phrase 'jñāna-mayaṁ tapaḥ' (tapas made of knowledge) creates a ring-composition spanning the entire Muṇḍaka Upanishad: First appearance (1.1.9): at the very beginning of the teaching, when the Upanishad introduces Brahman: 'yaḥ sarva-jñaḥ sarva-vit yasya jñāna-mayaṁ tapaḥ' — 'He who is omniscient, all-knowing, whose tapas is made of knowledge.' This is the thesis — the opening declaration. Final appearance (3.2.2): near the end of the Upanishad, the same phrase returns — closing the circle. The thesis is restated, now enriched by everything taught in between (the two kinds of knowledge, the fire-rituals, the bow-and-arrow meditation, the two birds, the knower's portrait, the river-ocean simile, 'brahma-vid brahmaiva bhavati'). What 'jñāna-maya tapas' means: (1) Brahman's creative force is intelligent, not mechanical — it is tapas whose very substance is jñāna (knowledge). (2) This distinguishes the Upanishadic view from both materialism (creation from blind matter) and voluntarism (creation from arbitrary will). Creation is the self-expression of omniscient consciousness. (3) The aspirant's tapas should mirror Brahman's tapas — it too should be 'jñāna-maya' — saturated with understanding, not mere mechanical austerity.

dp.q: 🔍 Nāma-rūpa — the philosophical significance of 'name and form'
dp.a:
नाम-रूप (name and form) उपनिषद् दर्शन की सर्वाधिक मूलभूत अवधारणाओं में से एक है। नाम क्या है? = किसी वस्तु की अवधारणात्मक पहचान — उसे क्या कहते हैं, कैसे वर्गीकृत करते हैं — मानसिक विभेदन का सिद्धान्त। रूप क्या है? = किसी वस्तु का ऐन्द्रिय प्रकटन — आकार, रंग, बनावट — प्रत्यक्ष विभेदन का सिद्धान्त। दोनों मिलकर = सम्पूर्ण दृश्य जगत्। उपनिषद् की शिक्षा: नाम-रूप स्वतन्त्र नहीं — ब्रह्म 'से' उत्पन्न ('तस्मात्... जायते')। जैसे तरंगें समुद्र से — तरंगें सत्य हैं 'तरंग रूप में' किन्तु मूलतः जल। छान्दोग्य (6.3.2-3): तीन तत्त्व (तेज, आप, पृथिवी) नाम-रूप में विभेदित — त्रिवृत्करण। बृहदारण्यक (1.4.7): 'यह तब अव्याकृत (अविभेदित) था; नाम-रूप से व्याकृत (विभेदित) हुआ।' नाम-रूप = ब्रह्म पर अध्यारोपण (शंकर) / ब्रह्म का वास्तविक विकास (रामानुज)।

Eng: The pair 'nāma-rūpa' (name and form) is one of the most fundamental concepts in Upanishadic philosophy: What are nāma and rūpa? (1) Nāma (name) = the conceptual identity of a thing — what it is called, how it is classified, its place in the mental map of the world. Nāma is the principle of mental differentiation. (2) Rūpa (form) = the sensory appearance of a thing — its shape, colour, texture, the way it presents itself to the senses. Rūpa is the principle of perceptual differentiation. (3) Together, nāma-rūpa = the entire phenomenal world — every object, every being, every event has a name (conceptual identity) and a form (perceptual appearance). The Upanishadic teaching: nāma-rūpa is not self-existent — it arises FROM Brahman ('tasmāt … nāma rūpam … jāyate'). The world of differentiated things emerges from the undifferentiated Brahman, much as waves arise from the ocean. The waves are real AS waves, but they are ultimately water. Key parallels: (1) Chāndogya (6.3.2-3): the three elements (tejas, āpas, pṛthivī) differentiate into nāma-rūpa through their mutual combinations — the 'trivṛt-karaṇa' (triplication). (2) Bṛhadāraṇyaka (1.4.7): 'This was then undifferentiated (avyākṛta); it became differentiated (vyākṛta) by nāma-rūpa.' (3) Buddhist parallel: nāma-rūpa appears as a link in the twelve-fold chain of dependent origination (pratītya-samutpāda) — though with a different metaphysical framework.

sk: तदेतत्सत्यं मन्त्रेषु कर्माणि कवयो यान्यपश्यंस्तानि त्रेतायां बहुधा सन्ततानि तान्याचरथ नियतं सत्यकामा एष वः पन्थाः सुकृतस्य लोके ||
ro: tat · etat · satyaṁ · mantreṣu · karmāṇi · kavayaḥ · yāni · apaśyan · tāni · tretāyāṁ · bahudhā · santatāni · tāni · ācaratha · niyataṁ · satya-kāmāḥ · eṣaḥ · vaḥ · panthāḥ · sukṛtasya · loke ||
hi: वह (तत्) यह (एतत्) सत्य (truth) है। मन्त्रों में (mantreṣu) कवियों (kavayaḥ / seers) ने जो कर्माणि (rites/actions) अपश्यन् (saw / perceived) — वे (तानि) त्रेतायां (in the Tretā fire / three-fold fire) बहुधा (in many ways) सन्ततानि (spread out / elaborated) हैं। उन्हें (तानि) नियतम् (steadily / faithfully) आचरथ (practise / perform), हे सत्यकामाः (lovers of truth / seekers of truth)! यह (एषः) तुम्हारा (वः) पन्थाः (path) है — सुकृतस्य लोके (to the world of good deeds / the world won by merit)।
en: This is the truth (tat etat satyam). The rites (karmāṇi) which the seers (kavayaḥ) saw (apaśyan) in the mantras — those are spread out (santatāni) in many ways (bahudhā) in the Tretā fire (tretāyām). Practise them (tāni ācaratha) faithfully (niyatam), O lovers of truth (satya-kāmāḥ)! This (eṣaḥ) is your (vaḥ) path (panthāḥ) to the world of merit (sukṛtasya loke).

ws.e: in the mantras / in Vedic hymns

ws.h: त्रेता अग्नि में / त्रिविध अग्नि में
ws.e: in the Tretā fire / threefold fire

ws.h: अनेक प्रकार से / विविध रूपों में

ws.e: lovers of truth / seekers of truth
in the world / to the world

gr:
व्याकरण: तत् एतत् सत्यम् — 'तत्' (वह) + 'एतत्' (यह) = दूरस्थ और निकटस्थ सर्वनामों का संयोग — 'वह-यह सत्य है' — निकट और दूर दोनों में सत्य। मन्त्रेषु — 'मन्त्र' का सप्तमी बहुवचन — 'वैदिक ऋचाओं में।' कर्माणि — 'कर्मन्' का प्रथमा/द्वितीया बहुवचन — 'यज्ञ-कर्म।' कवयः — 'कवि' का प्रथमा बहुवचन — 'ऋषि / द्रष्टा' — वे जिन्होंने मन्त्र 'देखे' (दृष्ट), रचे नहीं। अपश्यन् — √दृश् (पश्य्) का लङ् लकार बहुवचन — 'उन्होंने देखा।' त्रेतायाम् — 'त्रेता' = त्रिविध अग्नि (गार्हपत्य, आहवनीय, दक्षिणाग्नि) — सप्तमी — 'त्रेता अग्नि में।' बहुधा — अव्यय — 'अनेक प्रकार से।' सन्ततानि — सम् + √तन् (फैलाना) — 'विस्तृत / फैले हुए।' आचरथ — आ + √चर् (चलना/आचरण करना) — लोट् लकार, मध्यम पुरुष बहुवचन — 'आचरण करो!' — आदेश। नियतम् — नि + √यम् (नियन्त्रित करना) — 'नियमपूर्वक।' सत्यकामाः — सत्य + काम — तत्पुरुष — 'जिनकी काम (इच्छा) सत्य (truth) है।' पन्थाः — 'पथिन्' का प्रथमा एकवचन — 'मार्ग।' सुकृतस्य लोके — सु + कृत = 'अच्छा किया हुआ / पुण्य'; षष्ठी तत्पुरुष — 'पुण्य-लोक में।' यह मन्त्र तृतीय बार (2.2.8, 3.1.7, 3.2.3) आता है — कर्मकाण्ड-मार्ग को सम्मान सहित प्रमाणित करता है।
Eng: 'Tat etat satyam' = that-this is truth. 'Kavayaḥ apaśyan' = the seers SAW (not composed) the rites in the mantras. 'Tretāyām' = in the threefold fire. 'Ācaratha' (loṭ lakāra, madhyama puruṣa bahuvacana) = imperative 'practise!' 'Satya-kāmāḥ' = tatpuruṣa — those whose desire is truth. 'Sukṛtasya loke' = the world of merit. Third repetition (2.2.8, 3.1.7, 3.2.3) validates the ritual path with respect.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — कर्मकाण्ड-मार्ग (ritual path) = वैध (valid) किन्तु अपरा (lower)। 'सुकृतस्य लोके' = पुण्य-लोक — स्वर्ग — किन्तु अनित्य (temporary)। मन्त्र कर्मकाण्ड का सम्मान करता है — किन्तु अगले मन्त्र उससे ऊपर (beyond it) ले जाएँगे।
advaita.en: Shankara says the ritual path = valid but lower. 'Sukṛtasya loke' = worlds of merit — heaven — but temporary. The mantra respects the ritual path but the next mantras will lead beyond it.
advaita.ins: The ritual path is real and honoured — 'practise it faithfully, O lovers of truth!' But where does it lead? To the world of merit — which is temporary. What follows will show a path beyond — beyond merit, beyond worlds, to the imperishable itself.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — कर्मकाण्ड = भक्ति-मार्ग (devotional path) का अंग (limb)। 'सत्यकामाः' = भगवद्-प्रेमी (God-lovers)। कर्म-मार्ग = भगवद्-सेवा (service to God) — भगवान् को अर्पित (offered to God) हो तो श्रेष्ठ।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says ritual path = a limb of the devotional path. 'Satya-kāmāḥ' = God-lovers. Ritual path = service to God — if offered to God, it is excellent.
vishisht.ins: The rituals the seers saw — they're real paths. But offer them to God, and they become something more. Don't perform them for merit alone — perform them as service. That transforms the path from leading to heaven to leading to God.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — 'कर्माणि' = बाह्य अनुष्ठान (external rituals) — चेतना-विकास (consciousness-evolution) की प्रारम्भिक अवस्था। 'सत्यकामाः' = सत्य के अन्वेषक — जो सत्य चाहते हैं, उनके लिए कर्मकाण्ड प्रथम सोपान (first step)।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says 'karmāṇi' = external rituals — an initial stage of consciousness-evolution. 'Satya-kāmāḥ' = seekers of truth — for those who want truth, ritual is the first step.
aurobindo.ins: The rituals are real — the seers saw them. But they're the first step, not the last. For you who love truth, begin here — with disciplined practice, with the threefold fire. But know that the path doesn't end at the world of merit. It continues upward.

dp.q: 🔍 The Muṇḍaka's treatment of ritual — respect without ultimacy
dp.a:
मुण्डक उपनिषद् का वैदिक कर्मकाण्ड के प्रति दृष्टिकोण अनूठा है — सम्मान किन्तु अन्तिमता नहीं। आलोचना (1.2.7-10): 'प्लवा ह्येते अदृढा यज्ञरूपाः' (1.2.7) — 'ये यज्ञ-रूप नावें दुर्बल हैं' — संसार-सागर पार करने में असमर्थ। यज्ञ-प्रेमियों को 'मूढ' कहा जो 'श्रेष्ठ प्राप्त कर लिया' मानते हैं (1.2.9)। प्रमाणन (3.2.3): यही मन्त्र कर्मकाण्ड को वैध ठहराता है — 'नियतं आचरथ, हे सत्यकामाः!' समाधान: (1) आलोचना उन पर जो कर्मकाण्ड को सर्वोच्च मानें — अकेला पर्याप्त समझें। (2) प्रमाणन कर्मकाण्ड को वास्तविक मार्ग बताता है — 'सुकृतस्य लोके' (पुण्य-लोक) तक। (3) किन्तु तत्काल बाद उपनिषद् उससे आगे ले जाता है — अक्षर, ब्रह्म, 'सत्यमेव जयते' की ओर। शैक्षणिक रणनीति: शिष्य की वर्तमान साधना (कर्मकाण्ड) का सम्मान → उसकी वैधता की पुष्टि → फिर धीरे-धीरे उससे परे मार्गदर्शन — अस्वीकृति नहीं, अतिक्रमण।

Eng: The Muṇḍaka Upanishad has a distinctive relationship with Vedic ritual: The critique (1.2.7-10): in its first Muṇḍaka, the Upanishad delivers one of the sharpest critiques of ritual in Upanishadic literature — 'plavā hy ete adṛḍhā yajña-rūpāḥ' (1.2.7) — 'Frail indeed are those boats, the ritual forms.' Rituals are called 'frail boats' that cannot cross the ocean of saṁsāra. Those who delight in ritual are 'fools who think they have reached the highest' (1.2.9). The validation (3.2.3): yet THIS verse validates the ritual path — 'practise them faithfully, O lovers of truth!' How do we reconcile the critique with the validation? The resolution: (1) The critique targets those who mistake the ritual path for the highest — those who think ritual alone is sufficient. (2) The validation affirms the ritual path as a real path — it leads to 'sukṛtasya loke' (the world of merit). (3) But the Upanishad immediately follows this verse with teachings that point BEYOND the ritual path — to the imperishable, to Brahman, to 'satyameva jayate.' The pedagogical strategy: honour the student's current practice (ritual), affirm its validity, then gently lead them beyond it. This is the Upanishadic method — not rejection but transcendence.

dp.q: 🔍 'Satya-kāmāḥ' — the qualification of the seeker
dp.a:
'सत्यकामाः' (हे सत्य-प्रेमियो!) साधक की अनिवार्य योग्यता प्रकट करता है। सत्यकाम क्या है? सत्य (truth) + काम (desire/love) = जिसकी गहनतम इच्छा सत्य हो — जो सत्य का केवल अध्ययन नहीं, सत्य से प्रेम करता हो। छान्दोग्य का सत्यकाम (4.4): सत्यकाम जाबाल — गुरु हारिद्रुमत गौतम के समक्ष अपने पिता का नाम ईमानदारी से अज्ञात बताया — गौतम बोले: 'ब्राह्मण ही ऐसा सत्य बोल सकता है — समिधा लाओ, दीक्षा देता हूँ।' सत्यकाम की सत्यनिष्ठा ही उसकी योग्यता — न जन्म, न विद्या, न कर्मकाण्डीय शुद्धता। मुण्डक में अनुप्रयोग: 'सत्यकामाः' सम्बोधित शिष्य अपनी इच्छा (desire for truth) से योग्य हैं — मार्ग सत्य-प्रेमियों के लिए खुला — जो सत्य चाहते हैं उन्हें कर्मकाण्ड से ज्ञान तक, पुण्य-लोक से अक्षर तक पहुँचाएगा।

Eng: The address 'satya-kāmāḥ' (O lovers of truth) reveals the essential qualification for the spiritual path: What is satya-kāma? satya (truth) + kāma (desire/love) = one whose deepest desire is truth. Not one who merely studies truth, or talks about truth, or ritually invokes truth — but one who desires truth, who loves truth, whose fundamental orientation is toward the real. The Chāndogya's Satyakāma (4.4): the story of Satyakāma Jābāla is the locus classicus. When asked his lineage by the teacher Hāridrumata Gautama, Satyakāma honestly confesses that he doesn't know his father's name — his mother Jabālā told him she doesn't know. Gautama's response: 'None but a Brāhmaṇa could speak thus. Bring the fuel, my boy; I will initiate you. You have not swerved from truth.' Satyakāma's truthfulness IS his qualification — not birth, not learning, not ritual purity, but the love of truth. The Muṇḍaka's application: the students addressed as 'satya-kāmāḥ' are qualified by their desire — their love of truth. The path is open to those who genuinely seek. The Upanishad's confidence is: if you truly desire truth, the path will take you there — from ritual to knowledge, from merit-worlds to the imperishable.

sk: कामान्यः कामयते मन्यमानः स कामभिर्जायते तत्र तत्र पर्याप्तकामस्य कृतात्मनस्तु इहैव सर्वे प्रविलीयन्ति कामाः ||
ro: kāmān · yaḥ · kāmayate · manyamānaḥ · saḥ · kāmabhiḥ · jāyate · tatra · tatra · paryāpta-kāmasya · kṛta-ātmanaḥ · tu · iha · eva · sarve · pravilīyanti · kāmāḥ ||
hi: कामान् (desires / कामनाओं को) जो (यः) कामयते (desires / चाहता है) मन्यमानः (thinking [himself to be the doer/enjoyer] / अपने को कर्ता-भोक्ता मानता हुआ) — वह (सः) कामभिः (by/with desires / कामनाओं सहित) तत्र तत्र (here and there / यहाँ-वहाँ / विभिन्न योनियों में) जायते (is born / जन्म लेता है)। पर्याप्तकामस्य (of one whose desires are fulfilled / जिसकी कामनाएँ पूर्ण हो गई हैं) कृतात्मनः (of the self-realised one / कृतार्थ आत्मा वाले) तु (but / किन्तु) इह एव (right here / यहीं) सर्वे कामाः (all desires / सभी कामनाएँ) प्रविलीयन्ति (dissolve completely / पूर्णतया विलीन हो जाती हैं)।
en: He who desires desires (kāmān kāmayate), thinking [himself to be the agent] (manyamānaḥ) — he is born (jāyate) here and there (tatra tatra) along with [his] desires (kāmabhiḥ). But (tu) for the one whose desires are fulfilled (paryāpta-kāmasya), the self-realised one (kṛta-ātmanaḥ), all desires (sarve kāmāḥ) dissolve completely (pravilīyanti) right here (iha eva).

ws.e: thinking oneself to be the agent

ws.h: जन्म लेता है / उत्पन्न होता है

ws.e: here and there / in various wombs

ws.h: जिसकी कामनाएँ पूर्ण हो गई हैं

gr:
व्याकरण: कामान् — 'काम' का द्वितीया बहुवचन — 'कामनाओं को' — कर्म कारक। कामयते — √कम् (चाहना) आत्मनेपद — 'चाहता है।' 'कामान् कामयते' = जानबूझकर पुनरुक्ति — कामना की कामना — चक्र का संकेत। मन्यमानः — √मन् (मानना) शानच् प्रत्यय — 'मानता हुआ' — अहंकार: 'मैं कर्ता, मैं भोक्ता।' सः — सर्वनाम प्रथमा — 'वह।' कामभिः — तृतीया बहुवचन — 'कामनाओं सहित / द्वारा' — कामनाएँ साधन भी हैं और संगी भी। जायते — √जन् आत्मनेपद — 'जन्म लेता है।' तत्र तत्र — द्विरुक्ति — 'यहाँ-वहाँ' — अनेक योनियाँ, अनेक लोक। पर्याप्तकामस्य — परि + आप् + त + काम — षष्ठी — 'जिसकी कामनाएँ पूर्ण / तृप्त।' कृतात्मनः — कृत + आत्मन् — बहुव्रीहि — षष्ठी — 'जिसने आत्मा को सिद्ध किया है।' तु — अव्यय — 'किन्तु' — विपरीत स्थिति का संकेत। इह एव — 'इह' = यहीं + 'एव' = ही — 'इसी जीवन में, इसी शरीर में' — जीवन्मुक्ति। प्रविलीयन्ति — प्र + वि + √ली (लीन होना) — 'पूर्णतया विलीन' — उपसर्गों का त्रय (प्र+वि) पूर्णता सूचित करता है। कामाः — प्रथमा बहुवचन — 'सभी कामनाएँ' — कर्तृ कारक।
Eng: 'Kāmān kāmayate' = deliberate redundancy — desiring desires — the loop. 'Manyamānaḥ' (√man, śānac) = thinking oneself the agent — ego-identification is the root. 'Tatra tatra' = reduplication for 'here and there.' 'Paryāpta-kāmasya' (pari+āp+ta+kāma, ṣaṣṭhī) = one whose desires are fulfilled. 'Kṛtātmanaḥ' = bahuvrīhi — one whose Self is accomplished. 'Pravilīyanti' (pra+vi+√lī) = triple-prefix dissolution — utterly dissolve. 'Iha eva' = right here — jīvan-mukti.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — 'मन्यमानः' = अहंकार (ego) — 'मैं कर्ता हूँ, मैं भोक्ता हूँ' — यह भ्रम (delusion) पुनर्जन्म (rebirth) का कारण। 'पर्याप्तकामस्य कृतात्मनः' = जिसने आत्मा को जाना — उसकी सभी कामनाएँ इहैव (right here) विलीन — पुनर्जन्म नहीं। कामना = बन्धन (bondage)। कामना-निवृत्ति = मोक्ष।
advaita.en: Shankara says 'manyamānaḥ' = the ego — 'I am the doer, I am the enjoyer' — this delusion is the cause of rebirth. 'Paryāpta-kāmasya kṛtātmanaḥ' = one who has known the Self — all desires dissolve right here — no rebirth. Desire = bondage. Cessation of desire = mokṣa.
advaita.ins: You desire — and you're reborn. Not because desire is punished, but because desire is the engine. Each unfulfilled wish pulls you into another body, another life, another round. But when you find the Self — the source of all satisfaction — every desire dissolves. Not in some future life. Right here. Right now. The engine stops.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — 'कामभिः जायते' = भगवान् से विमुख (turned away from God) जीव — कामनाओं द्वारा संसार-चक्र (cycle of rebirth) में घूमता है। 'पर्याप्तकामस्य' = भक्त जिसने भगवान् को प्राप्त किया — उसकी सब कामनाएँ तृप्त — भगवान् में सर्व-तृप्ति (all satisfaction in God)।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says 'kāmabhiḥ jāyate' = the soul turned away from God — cycles through rebirth driven by desires. 'Paryāpta-kāmasya' = the devotee who has attained God — all desires are satisfied — all satisfaction is in God.
vishisht.ins: Desire without God drives you from birth to birth. But when you find God, every desire finds its rest. Not because desires are crushed — because they're fulfilled. God is what every desire was secretly looking for. Find Him, and the search ends — right here, in this life.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — 'मन्यमानः' = अहंकार-चेतना (ego-consciousness) — सीमित 'मैं' (limited 'I')। 'कामभिः जायते' = इच्छा-शक्ति (desire-force) = चेतना का विकृत रूप (distorted form of consciousness) — जो पुनर्जन्म चक्र चलाता है। 'प्रविलीयन्ति' = चेतना-रूपान्तर (consciousness-transformation) से कामना विलीन — अहंकार गिरता है, चेतना मुक्त।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says 'manyamānaḥ' = ego-consciousness — the limited 'I'. 'Kāmabhiḥ jāyate' = desire-force = a distorted form of consciousness — which drives the cycle of rebirth. 'Pravilīyanti' = through consciousness-transformation, desire dissolves — the ego falls, consciousness is free.
aurobindo.ins: Desire is consciousness in distorted form — the ego grasping at objects, thinking itself the doer. This distortion drives rebirth. But when consciousness transforms — when you see through the ego to the Self behind it — desire doesn't need to be killed. It dissolves. Because what desire was reaching for, you already are.

dp.q: 🔍 'Kāmān kāmayate' — the loop of desire and rebirth
dp.a:
'कामान् यः कामयते' ('जो कामनाओं की कामना करता है') पुनर्जन्म की तन्त्ररचना अत्यन्त सूक्ष्मता से प्रकट करता है। चक्र: (1) कामना उत्पन्न → (2) अहंकार कामना से तादात्म्य ('मन्यमानः') → (3) कर्म कामना का अनुगमन → (4) कर्म-बीज बोए जाते हैं → (5) अतृप्त कामनाओं सहित मृत्यु → (6) अतृप्त कामनाएँ नए शरीर में ले जाती हैं ('तत्र तत्र जायते') → (7) नए शरीर में कामना पुनः → पुनरावृत्ति। 'मन्यमानः' क्यों कुंजी है? मन्त्र नहीं कहता कि अकेली कामना पुनर्जन्म देती है — कामना सहित 'मन्यमानः' (अहं-बोध)। कामना + अहंकार = बन्धन। गीता (3.27): 'प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः, अहंकार-विमूढात्मा कर्ताहमिति मन्यते।' बृहदारण्यक (4.4.5-6): 'जैसी कामना — वैसा संकल्प; जैसा संकल्प — वैसा कर्म; जैसा कर्म — वैसी गति।' कामना → संकल्प → कर्म → गति → पुनर्जन्म।

Eng: The phrase 'kāmān yaḥ kāmayate' ('he who desires desires') reveals the mechanism of rebirth with remarkable precision: The loop: (1) Desire arises → (2) The ego identifies with the desire ('manyamānaḥ') → (3) Action follows desire → (4) Karmic seeds are sown → (5) Death comes with unfulfilled desires → (6) The unfulfilled desires propel the soul into a new body ('tatra tatra jāyate') → (7) In the new body, desire arises again → repeat. Why 'manyamānaḥ' is the key: the mantra doesn't say desire alone causes rebirth — it says desire PLUS 'manyamānaḥ' (thinking oneself to be the agent/enjoyer). This is crucial: it's not desire per se that binds — it's desire combined with ego-identification. The Gītā (3.27) makes the same point: 'prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ, ahaṅkāra-vimūḍhātmā kartāham iti manyate' — 'Actions are performed by the guṇas of prakṛti, but the one deluded by ego thinks: I am the doer.' The Bṛhadāraṇyaka parallel (4.4.5-6): Yājñavalkya's teaching is virtually identical — 'As is one's desire (kāma), so is one's will (kratu); as is one's will, so is one's deed (karma); as is one's deed, so is one's destiny (gati).' Desire → will → action → destiny → rebirth. 'Tatra tatra' — 'here and there': the desirer is born in many places — human, animal, divine, hellish — according to the nature of the desires. The variety of births reflects the variety of desires.

dp.q: 🔍 'Ihaiva sarve pravilīyanti kāmāḥ' — liberation is here, not elsewhere
dp.a:
'इहैव सर्वे प्रविलीयन्ति कामाः' ('यहीं सभी कामनाएँ पूर्णतया विलीन हो जाती हैं') — एक क्रान्तिकारी घोषणा — मोक्ष इसी जीवन में, मृत्यु के बाद नहीं। 'इह एव' — यहीं: 'इह' (यहाँ) + 'एव' (ही) — बल अमिथ्य — स्वर्ग में नहीं, अगले जन्म में नहीं, मरणोपरान्त नहीं — यहीं, इस शरीर में, इस जीवन में — जीवन्मुक्ति। 'प्रविलीयन्ति' — पूर्ण विलय: प्र + वि + √ली = बिना शेष विलय — कामनाएँ दबती नहीं, सुप्त नहीं होतीं — विलीन — नमक पानी में, कोहरा धूप में। कैसे विलीन? दमन से नहीं — दबी कामनाएँ सुप्त रहकर लौटती हैं। थकान से नहीं — तृप्ति और कामना उत्पन्न करती है। स्रोत पर तृप्ति से — आत्मा ही सब तृप्ति का स्रोत। जब आत्मा मिला (कृतात्मन्) — जड़ मिली — शाखाएँ स्वतः गिरीं। बृहदारण्यक (4.4.7): 'जैसे सर्प की केंचुली वल्मीक पर पड़ी — मृत, त्यागी — वैसे यह शरीर। किन्तु जो अशरीरी, अमृत, प्राण — वही ब्रह्म, वही ज्योतिः।'

Eng: The phrase 'iha eva sarve pravilīyanti kāmāḥ' ('right HERE all desires dissolve completely') makes a radical claim — liberation happens in this very life, not after death: 'Iha eva' — right here: the emphasis is unmistakable — 'iha' (here) + 'eva' (indeed/only). Not in heaven, not in a future life, not after death — but HERE, in this body, in this life. This is the Upanishadic concept of jīvan-mukti (liberation while living) — one need not wait for bodily death to be free. 'Pravilīyanti' — dissolve completely: the verb is emphatic. 'Pra-vi-lī' = to dissolve utterly, to merge away without residue. Desires don't merely weaken, become dormant, or go underground. They DISSOLVE — like salt in water, like mist in sunlight. Nothing remains. How do desires dissolve? Not by suppression — suppressed desires remain latent and resurface. Not by exhaustion — satisfying desires only creates more desires. But by fulfilment at the source. The Self IS the source of all satisfaction. Every desire is ultimately a desire for the Self — for completeness, for wholeness, for peace. When the Self is found (kṛta-ātman), the root from which all desires grow is reached. And when the root is reached, the branches (individual desires) naturally fall away. The Bṛhadāraṇyaka's beautiful image (4.4.7): 'As the slough of a snake lies on an ant-hill, dead and cast off, so lies this body. But that which is bodiless, immortal, prāṇa — that is Brahman, that is light.' When desires dissolve, what remains is not emptiness but fullness — the light of the Self.

sk: सत्येन लभ्यस्तपसा ह्येष आत्मा सम्यग्ज्ञानेन ब्रह्मचर्येण नित्यम् अन्तःशरीरे ज्योतिर्मयो हि शुभ्रो यं पश्यन्ति यतयः क्षीणदोषाः ||
ro: satyena · labhyaḥ · tapasā · hi · eṣaḥ · ātmā · samyag-jñānena · brahmacaryeṇa · nityam · antaḥ-śarīre · jyotir-mayaḥ · hi · śubhraḥ · yaṁ · paśyanti · yatayaḥ · kṣīṇa-doṣāḥ ||
hi: सत्येन (by truth / सत्य से), तपसा (by tapas / तप से), सम्यग्ज्ञानेन (by right knowledge / सम्यक् ज्ञान से), ब्रह्मचर्येण नित्यम् (by constant brahmacarya / निरन्तर ब्रह्मचर्य से) — यह (एषः) आत्मा (Self) लभ्यः (is attainable / प्राप्त होने योग्य) है। अन्तःशरीरे (within the body / शरीर के भीतर) ज्योतिर्मयः (made of light / ज्योतिर्मय) शुभ्रः (pure / resplendent) — जिसे (यं) यतयः (ascetics / साधक / strivers), क्षीणदोषाः (whose faults are destroyed / दोष-मुक्त), पश्यन्ति (see / दर्शन करते हैं)।
en: By truth (satyena), by tapas (tapasā), by right knowledge (samyag-jñānena), by constant brahmacarya (brahmacaryeṇa nityam) — this Self (eṣa ātmā) is attainable (labhyaḥ). Within the body (antaḥ-śarīre), [It is] made of light (jyotir-maya), pure/resplendent (śubhra) — which the ascetics (yatayaḥ), whose faults are destroyed (kṣīṇa-doṣāḥ), see (paśyanti).

ws.h: सम्यक् ज्ञान से / सही ज्ञान द्वारा
ws.e: by right knowledge / by correct understanding

gr:
व्याकरण: सत्येन — 'सत्य' का तृतीया (instrumental) — 'सत्य द्वारा' — प्रथम साधन। लभ्यः — √लभ् (प्राप्त करना) + यत् प्रत्यय — कर्मणि विशेषण — 'प्राप्य / प्राप्त होने योग्य।' तपसा — तृतीया — 'तप द्वारा' — द्वितीय साधन। हि — अव्यय — 'निश्चय ही' — बल। सम्यग्ज्ञानेन — सम्यक् + ज्ञान — तृतीया — 'सम्यक् (samyak) = सम्यक्/सम्पूर्ण/यथार्थ; ज्ञान = √ज्ञा (जानना)' — तृतीय साधन — 'सम्यक्' ज्ञान को विशिष्ट करता है — आंशिक, विकृत या केवल बौद्धिक ज्ञान अपर्याप्त। ब्रह्मचर्येण — ब्रह्मचर्य (ब्रह्म + चर् = ब्रह्म की ओर चलना) — तृतीया — चतुर्थ साधन। नित्यम् — अव्यय — 'निरन्तर' — ब्रह्मचर्य 'नित्य' (सदैव) होना चाहिए। अन्तःशरीरे — अन्तः (भीतर) + शरीर — सप्तमी — 'शरीर के भीतर' — आत्मा बाहर नहीं, भीतर। ज्योतिर्मयः — ज्योतिस् (प्रकाश) + मयट् — 'प्रकाश-स्वरूप' — आत्मा = स्वयंप्रकाश। शुभ्रः — √शुभ् (शोभित होना) — 'शुद्ध / उज्ज्वल।' यतयः — 'यति' (√यत् = प्रयत्न करना) का प्रथमा बहुवचन — 'साधक / प्रयत्नशील।' क्षीणदोषाः — क्षीण (√क्षि = नष्ट करना — भूतकृदन्त) + दोष — बहुव्रीहि — 'जिनके दोष क्षय हो गए।' चार साधन चार आयाम: सत्य = नैतिक, तप = रूपान्तरकारी, सम्यग्ज्ञान = बोधात्मक, ब्रह्मचर्य = ऊर्जा-संरक्षण। यह मन्त्र अगले 'सत्यमेव जयते' की आधारशिला।
Eng: Four instruments in instrumental case: satyena, tapasā, samyag-jñānena, brahmacaryeṇa. 'Labhyaḥ' (√labh + yat) = obtainable (karmaṇi). 'Jyotir-mayaḥ' = mayaṭ suffix on jyotis — made of light. 'Kṣīṇa-doṣāḥ' = bahuvrīhi compound — whose faults are destroyed. The fourfold sādhana: truth (ethical), tapas (transformative), right knowledge (cognitive), brahmacarya (energetic).

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — चार साधन: (1) सत्य = नैतिक आधार। (2) तप = अन्तर्मुखता (inwardness) — इन्द्रिय-निग्रह (sense-restraint)। (3) सम्यग्ज्ञान = 'अहं ब्रह्मास्मि' (I am Brahman) का यथार्थ बोध। (4) ब्रह्मचर्य = वीर्य-रक्षा और शमदमादि। 'ज्योतिर्मयः' = आत्मा = स्वयंप्रकाश (self-luminous) — बाह्य प्रकाश की आवश्यकता नहीं।
advaita.en: Shankara says four means: (1) satya = moral foundation. (2) tapas = inwardness — sense-restraint. (3) samyag-jñāna = correct understanding of 'ahaṁ brahmāsmi' (I am Brahman). (4) brahmacarya = conservation of vital energy and mental disciplines. 'Jyotir-maya' = the Self = self-luminous — needs no external light.
advaita.ins: Four things will take you to the Self: truth, tapas, right knowledge, and brahmacarya. Not one alone — all four together. And what will you find? A light within your own body — not brought from outside but always there, always shining. You couldn't see it because your faults blocked the view. Remove them, and the light reveals itself.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — 'सत्येन लभ्यः' = भगवान् सत्य से प्राप्त होते हैं — सत्य = भक्ति का मूल (root of devotion)। 'ज्योतिर्मयः' = भगवान् = दिव्य ज्योति — शरीर के भीतर अन्तर्यामी (inner controller) रूप में विराजमान। 'क्षीणदोषाः' = जिन भक्तों के दोष (कर्म-वासना, अज्ञान) नष्ट — वे भगवद्-दर्शन (vision of God) करते हैं।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says 'satyena labhyaḥ' = God is attained by truth — truth = the root of devotion. 'Jyotir-maya' = the Lord = divine light — dwelling within the body as the inner controller (antaryāmī). 'Kṣīṇa-doṣāḥ' = those devotees whose faults (karmic impressions, ignorance) are destroyed — they behold God.
vishisht.ins: God is attained by truth, by tapas, by right knowledge, by devoted discipline. He lives within your body as pure light — the inner controller. Those whose faults have been burned away by practice — they see Him. The light was always there. Your faults were the only veil.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — चार साधन = चेतना-शुद्धि (consciousness-purification) के चार आयाम: सत्य (truth-consciousness), तप (concentration of consciousness-force), सम्यग्ज्ञान (integral knowledge), ब्रह्मचर्य (consecration of being)। 'ज्योतिर्मयः' = अतिमानसिक प्रकाश (supramental light) — शरीर में अवतरित (descended into the body)।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says four means = four dimensions of consciousness-purification: satya (truth-consciousness), tapas (concentration of consciousness-force), samyag-jñāna (integral knowledge), brahmacarya (consecration of being). 'Jyotir-maya' = supramental light — descended into the body.
aurobindo.ins: Four paths, one goal. Truth — not just not-lying but alignment with reality. Tapas — concentrated will. Right knowledge — not intellectual but integral, felt in every cell. Brahmacarya — consecrating your entire being to the divine. What you find is light within the body — the supramental consciousness, already there, waiting for your faults to clear.

dp.q: 🔍 The fourfold sādhana — truth, tapas, knowledge, brahmacarya
dp.a:
यह मन्त्र आत्म-प्राप्ति के चार साधन बताता है — मुण्डक का सर्वाधिक व्यवस्थित साधना-कथन। (1) सत्य: नैतिक आयाम — सत्य = (अ) सत्य वचन — जो है वह कहना, (ब) सत्य आचरण — यथार्थ के अनुकूल कर्म, (ग) सत्य अस्तित्व — आत्म-छल से मुक्ति। छान्दोग्य का सत्यकाम = आदर्श — सत्यनिष्ठा ही योग्यता। (2) तप: रूपान्तरकारी आयाम — संकेन्द्रित प्रयत्न, आत्म-अनुशासन, विकास हेतु कष्ट सहने की इच्छा। मुण्डक में तप = सृष्टिकारी (ब्रह्म का तप) और साधनात्मक (साधक का तप) दोनों। (3) सम्यग्ज्ञान: बोधात्मक आयाम — 'सम्यक्' = सही, सम्पूर्ण, प्रत्यक्ष — 1.1.5 में परिभाषित 'परा विद्या' — जिससे अक्षर ज्ञात हो — बौद्धिक या शास्त्रीय ज्ञान मात्र 'अपरा'। (4) ब्रह्मचर्य: ऊर्जापरक आयाम — ब्रह्मचर्य = ब्रह्म + चर् = ब्रह्म की ओर चलना — ओजस्-रक्षा, इन्द्रिय-संयम, गुरु-सान्निध्य, समग्र जीवन-समर्पण। चतुर्विध समन्वय: अकेला कोई पर्याप्त नहीं — सत्य बिना तप = शक्तिहीन; तप बिना ज्ञान = अन्ध; ज्ञान बिना ब्रह्मचर्य = बिखरा हुआ। चारों मिलकर कार्य करें।

Eng: This mantra prescribes four qualifications for attaining the Self — the most systematic sādhana statement in the Muṇḍaka: (1) Satya (truth): the moral dimension. Without truthfulness, spiritual practice is built on sand. Truth here means: (a) truthful speech — saying what is real, (b) truthful conduct — acting in alignment with reality, (c) truthful being — living without self-deception. The Chāndogya's Satyakāma is the model — his truthfulness WAS his qualification. (2) Tapas (austerity): the transformative dimension. Tapas = concentrated effort, self-discipline, the willingness to endure discomfort for growth. In the Muṇḍaka's vocabulary, tapas has appeared as both cosmic (Brahman's creative tapas) and personal (the aspirant's practice). (3) Samyag-jñāna (right knowledge): the cognitive dimension. Not just any knowledge but 'samyak' — correct, complete, direct. This is parā vidyā (higher knowledge) as defined in 1.1.5 — knowledge of 'that by which the imperishable is known.' Mere intellectual understanding or scriptural scholarship is aparā (lower). (4) Brahmacarya (self-discipline): the energetic dimension. Brahmacarya literally means 'conduct toward Brahman' — a life oriented toward the divine. It includes celibacy but is much broader: conservation of vital energy, restraint of the senses, living under a teacher's guidance, dedication of one's entire lifestyle to the goal. The fourfold integration: none of the four alone suffices. Truth without tapas lacks transformative power. Tapas without knowledge is blind. Knowledge without brahmacarya dissipates. All four must work together — moral purity (satya), concentrated effort (tapas), correct understanding (samyag-jñāna), and disciplined lifestyle (brahmacarya).

dp.q: 🔍 'Antaḥ-śarīre jyotir-mayaḥ' — the light within the body
dp.a:
'अन्तःशरीरे ज्योतिर्मयः' (शरीर के भीतर, प्रकाश-स्वरूप) — आत्मा को दूरस्थ पारलौकिकता में नहीं, यहीं शरीर में स्थापित करता है। निहितार्थ: आत्मा खोजने के लिए किसी अन्य लोक, दूरस्थ स्वर्ग, या शरीर-अतिक्रमण की आवश्यकता नहीं — आत्मा 'अन्तःशरीरे' — शरीर के भीतर — सदा से विद्यमान। 'ज्योतिर्मय' क्यों? (1) स्वयंप्रकाशता: आत्मा को बाह्य प्रकाश की आवश्यकता नहीं — स्वयं प्रकाश है। कठ (2.2.15): 'न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं... तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति।' (2) चेतना = प्रकाश: उपनिषद् की रूपक-प्रणाली में ज्योतिस् = चित् — 'प्रकाश-स्वरूप' = चेतना-स्वरूप। (3) शुभ्र = निर्मल — शरीर की अशुद्धियों के बीच भी आत्मा शुभ्र — दर्पण पर धूल, पर दर्पण अक्षत। कौन देखता है? 'यतयः क्षीणदोषाः' — जिनके दोष (काम, क्रोध, लोभ, मोह, मद, मात्सर्य) नष्ट — प्रकाश सदा है — बाधा हमारी अशुद्धि — अशुद्धि हटाओ, प्रकाश स्वयं दिखे।

Eng: The phrase 'antaḥ-śarīre jyotir-mayaḥ' (within the body, made of light) places the Self not in a transcendent beyond but right here, inside the body: The implication: you don't need to travel to another world, reach a distant heaven, or transcend the body to find the Self. The Self is 'antaḥ-śarīre' — within the body. It's not brought from outside; it's already there, always has been, always will be. Why 'jyotir-maya' (made of light)? (1) Self-luminosity: the Self doesn't need external illumination — it IS light. The Kaṭha (2.2.15) makes this explicit: 'na tatra sūryo bhāti na candra-tārakam, nemā vidyuto bhānti kuto'yam agniḥ / tam eva bhāntam anubhāti sarvaṁ, tasya bhāsā sarvam idaṁ vibhāti' — 'There the sun doesn't shine, nor the moon, nor stars, nor lightning, much less fire. Everything shines after Him; by His light, all this is illumined.' (2) Consciousness = light: in the Upanishadic metaphor system, light (jyotis) = consciousness (cit). To say the Self is 'made of light' is to say it IS consciousness — pure, luminous, self-aware. (3) 'Śubhra' (pure/resplendent): the Self-light is not mixed with darkness — it is pure, brilliant, unstained. Even while dwelling within the body (with all its impurities), the Self remains śubhra. Who sees it? 'Yatayaḥ kṣīṇa-doṣāḥ' — ascetics/strivers whose faults are destroyed. The light is always there; the obstacle is our own inner impurities. Remove the faults (through the fourfold sādhana), and the light that was always shining becomes visible.

sk: सत्यमेव जयते नानृतं सत्येन पन्था विततो देवयानः येनाक्रमन्त्यृषयो ह्याप्तकामा यत्र तत्सत्यस्य परमं निधानम् ||
ro: satyam · eva · jayate · na · anṛtaṁ · satyena · panthāḥ · vitataḥ · deva-yānaḥ · yena · ākramanti · ṛṣayaḥ · hi · āpta-kāmāḥ · yatra · tat · satyasya · paramaṁ · nidhānam ||
hi: सत्यम् एव जयते (truth alone prevails / सत्य ही जीतता है) — न अनृतम् (not untruth / असत्य नहीं)। सत्येन (by truth / सत्य से) पन्थाः (the path / मार्ग) विततः (is spread out / विस्तृत) देवयानः (the path of the gods / देवयान-मार्ग) — येन (by which) ऋषयः (the sages) आप्तकामाः (whose desires are fulfilled / पूर्णकाम) आक्रमन्ति (ascend / journey / चढ़ते हैं) — यत्र (where) तत् सत्यस्य (of truth / सत्य का) परमं निधानम् (supreme treasure / परम निधान) [है]।
en: Truth alone prevails (satyam eva jayate), not untruth (na anṛtam). By truth (satyena) is spread out (vitataḥ) the path of the gods (deva-yānaḥ), by which the sages (ṛṣayaḥ), whose desires are fulfilled (āpta-kāmāḥ), ascend (ākramanti) — to where (yatra) is the supreme treasure (paramaṁ nidhānam) of truth (satyasya).

ws.e: the path of the gods / luminous path

gr:
व्याकरण: सत्यम् एव जयते — 'सत्यम्' = प्रथमा एकवचन; 'एव' = अवधारण (emphasis) — 'केवल / ही'; 'जयते' = √जि (जीतना) आत्मनेपद — 'विजयी होता है।' यह केवल नैतिक नहीं, तात्त्विक कथन — सत् (being/reality) ही अन्ततः विजयी। न अनृतम् — अन् + ऋत (ऋत = विश्व-सत्य/ऋत) — 'अनृत' = ऋत-विरोधी = असत्य/मिथ्या — 'असत्य [विजयी] नहीं [होता]।' सत्येन — तृतीया — 'सत्य द्वारा' — मार्ग 'सत्य से' बना है। पन्थाः — 'पथिन्' का प्रथमा एकवचन। विततः — वि + √तन् (फैलाना) — भूतकृदन्त — 'विस्तृत / फैला हुआ।' देवयानः — देव + यान (√या = जाना) — तत्पुरुष — 'देवों का मार्ग' — अनिवर्तन-मार्ग (path of no return)। आक्रमन्ति — आ + √क्रम् (कदम रखना) — 'चढ़ते हैं / आगे बढ़ते हैं।' आप्तकामाः — आप्त (√आप् = प्राप्त करना) + काम — बहुव्रीहि — 'जिन्होंने कामनाएँ प्राप्त कर लीं / पूर्णकाम।' सत्यस्य — षष्ठी — 'सत्य का।' परमं निधानम् — निधानम् = नि + √धा (रखना) — 'भण्डार / निधि / निवास' — 'सत्य का परम निधान' = ब्रह्म। यह मन्त्र भारत का राष्ट्रीय आदर्श वाक्य है — अशोक-स्तम्भ के नीचे देवनागरी में अंकित।
Eng: 'Satyam eva jayate' — 'satya' (nominative) + 'eva' (emphatic particle) + 'jayate' (√ji, ātmanepada). Not merely moral but metaphysical — sat (being) prevails over asat (non-being). 'Anṛtam' = an + ṛta (cosmic order). 'Deva-yānaḥ' = tatpuruṣa — the path of the gods / path of no return. 'Āpta-kāmāḥ' = bahuvrīhi — whose desires are fulfilled. 'Paramaṁ nidhānam' = the supreme treasure/repository of truth = Brahman. This is India's national motto.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — 'सत्यमेव जयते' = सत् (real / being) ही अन्ततः विजयी — असत् (unreal) = माया (illusion) = पराजित। यह नैतिक (ethical) और आध्यात्मिक (metaphysical) दोनों कथन है। 'देवयान' = ज्ञान-मार्ग (path of knowledge) — ब्रह्म-लोक तक। 'परमं निधानम्' = निर्गुण ब्रह्म (attributeless Brahman) — परम सत्य — जहाँ कोई लौटकर नहीं आता।
advaita.en: Shankara says 'satyameva jayate' = sat (the real/being) alone ultimately prevails — asat (the unreal) = māyā (illusion) = is defeated. This is both ethical and metaphysical. 'Deva-yāna' = the path of knowledge — to Brahma-loka. 'Paramaṁ nidhānam' = nirguṇa Brahman (attributeless Brahman) — the supreme truth — from which there is no return.
advaita.ins: Truth alone prevails. Not eventually — ultimately. The real outlasts the unreal, being outlasts seeming, consciousness outlasts ignorance. The path to Brahman is made of truth — laid out by truth, walked in truth, leading to the supreme treasure of truth. The sages who walk it need nothing — because they've found the Self, and in the Self, all desires are already fulfilled.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — 'सत्यमेव जयते' = भगवान् (God) = सत्य (truth) — वही अन्ततः विजयी। 'देवयान' = भक्ति-मार्ग (path of devotion) — भगवत्-प्राप्ति (God-attainment) का मार्ग। 'परमं निधानम्' = भगवान् का दिव्य धाम (divine abode / Vaikuṇṭha) — जहाँ भक्त शाश्वत आनन्द (eternal bliss) भोगते हैं।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says 'satyameva jayate' = God = truth — He alone ultimately prevails. 'Deva-yāna' = the path of devotion — the path to God-attainment. 'Paramaṁ nidhānam' = the Lord's divine abode (Vaikuṇṭha) — where devotees enjoy eternal bliss.
vishisht.ins: Truth prevails — and God is truth. The path of the gods is the path of devotion — laid out by truth, walked in love, leading to God's own abode. The sages who walk it are fulfilled — not because they got everything they wanted, but because they found the One who IS everything they wanted.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — 'सत्यमेव जयते' = सत्य-चेतना (truth-consciousness) ही अन्ततः विजयी — असत्य = अज्ञान (ignorance) = चेतना का अवरोहण (involution)। 'देवयान' = चेतना-आरोहण (ascent of consciousness) — मनोमय (mental) से अतिमानसिक (supramental) तक। 'परमं निधानम्' = सच्चिदानन्द (sat-cit-ānanda) — सत्य का परम धाम।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says 'satyameva jayate' = truth-consciousness alone ultimately prevails — untruth = ignorance = the involution of consciousness. 'Deva-yāna' = the ascent of consciousness — from mental to supramental. 'Paramaṁ nidhānam' = sat-cit-ānanda — the supreme abode of truth.
aurobindo.ins: Truth alone prevails — because truth is the nature of consciousness, and consciousness is the nature of reality. The path of the gods is the path of consciousness ascending — from mind to overmind to supermind. The sages who walk it have fulfilled all desires not by satisfying them but by reaching the source — sat-cit-ānanda, the supreme treasure of truth.

dp.q: 🔍 'Satyameva Jayate' — from Upanishad to national motto
dp.a:
'सत्यमेव जयते' का एक उल्लेखनीय इतिहास है — गूढ उपनिषद् शिक्षा से भारत के राष्ट्रीय आदर्श वाक्य तक। मुण्डक में: यह पद ब्रह्म-प्राप्ति-मार्ग की अन्तिम शिक्षा के सन्दर्भ में आता है — प्रथमतः तात्त्विक कथन, द्वितीयतः नैतिक — 'सत्य' = जो वास्तव में है (सत् = being) — असत्य पर सत्ता का विजय। अंगीकरण: 1950 में नव-स्वतन्त्र भारत गणराज्य ने 'सत्यमेव जयते' को राष्ट्रीय आदर्श वाक्य के रूप में अपनाया — सारनाथ के अशोक-स्तम्भ सिंह-शीर्ष (तृतीय शती ई.पू.) के नीचे देवनागरी में अंकित। राजनैतिक अनुनाद: महात्मा गाँधी का 'सत्याग्रह' (सत्य-बल) इसी उपनिषद् परम्परा से — गाँधी के लिए सत्य केवल नैतिक मूल्य नहीं, ब्रह्माण्डीय शक्ति — अहिंसक सत्य का हिंसक असत्य पर विजय = 'सत्यमेव जयते, न अनृतम्।' दार्शनिक गहराई: (1) नैतिक: सत्याचरण का छल पर विजय। (2) तात्त्विक: सत् (being) का असत् (appearance) पर। (3) मोक्षपरक: सत्य-मार्ग (देवयान) = परम निधान; असत्य-मार्ग = पुनर्जन्म। (4) सृष्टिपरक: विश्व ऋत (सत्य-व्यवस्था) पर आधारित — असत्य अस्थायी विचलन।

Eng: The phrase 'satyameva jayate' has a remarkable history — from an esoteric Upanishadic teaching to the national motto of India: In the Muṇḍaka: the phrase occurs in the context of the final teaching on the path to Brahman. It is a metaphysical statement first and a moral statement second. 'Satya' here is not just honesty — it is 'that which is real' (sat = being). The mantra says: reality prevails over appearance, the true over the false. This is the nature of things — truth doesn't need to 'fight' to prevail; it prevails because it IS. The adoption: in 1950, the newly independent Republic of India adopted 'Satyameva Jayate' as its national motto. It was inscribed in Devanāgarī script beneath the Lion Capital of Ashoka (from Sarnath, 3rd century BCE), which became the national emblem. The political resonance: Mahatma Gandhi's philosophy of satyāgraha ('truth-force' / 'holding to truth') drew directly on this Upanishadic tradition. For Gandhi, truth was not merely a moral value but a cosmic force — the same force the Muṇḍaka describes. His conviction that non-violent truth would ultimately prevail over violent untruth echoed 'satyameva jayate, na anṛtam.' The philosophical depth: the phrase operates at multiple levels: (1) Ethical: truthful conduct prevails over deceit. (2) Metaphysical: sat (being/reality) prevails over asat (non-being/appearance). (3) Soteriological: the path of truth (satya → deva-yāna) leads to the supreme treasure, while the path of untruth leads to rebirth. (4) Cosmological: the universe is grounded in ṛta (cosmic order/truth) — disorder and falsehood are temporary deviations from the fundamental order.

dp.q: 🔍 The deva-yāna — the path of the gods
dp.a:
देवयान (देवों का मार्ग / ज्योतिर्मार्ग) उपनिषद् के मोक्ष-सिद्धान्त की प्रमुख अवधारणाओं में से एक है। दो मार्ग: (1) देवयान = अनिवर्तन-मार्ग — ब्रह्म की ओर — ज्ञानी और भक्त के लिए। (2) पितृयान = निवर्तन-मार्ग — चन्द्रलोक तक, फिर पुनर्जन्म — बिना ज्ञान के कर्मकाण्डियों के लिए। मार्ग-क्रम (छान्दोग्य 5.10, बृहदारण्यक 6.2): ज्वाला → दिन → शुक्लपक्ष → उत्तरायण → संवत्सर → सूर्य → चन्द्र → विद्युत् → अमानव पुरुष जो ब्रह्म तक ले जाता है। 'सत्येन विततः' का अर्थ: मार्ग 'सत्य से फैला हुआ' — सत्य ही मार्ग-पदार्थ — देवयान भौतिक दिशा नहीं बल्कि उत्तरोत्तर सत्य-बोध का मार्ग — प्रत्येक 'स्टेशन' (ज्वाला, सूर्य, विद्युत्) = चेतना-आरोहण की अवस्था। 'आप्तकामाः' — उनकी कामनाएँ 'प्राप्त' — हर सांसारिक इच्छा पूरी नहीं बल्कि आत्मा मिला — आत्मा में सब कुछ — तैत्तिरीय (2.1.1): 'आप्नोति सर्वान् कामान् सह ब्रह्मणा विपश्चिता।' 'परमं निधानम्' = 'सत्य का परम भण्डार' — गन्तव्य स्थान नहीं, सत्ता — सत्य का अक्षय कोष — जो कभी चुकता नहीं।

Eng: The 'deva-yāna' (path of the gods / luminous path) is one of the most important concepts in Upanishadic soteriology: Two paths: the Upanishads describe two post-mortem paths: (1) Deva-yāna (path of the gods) — the path of no-return, leading to Brahman. Reserved for those who have knowledge (jñāna) or devotion (bhakti). (2) Pitṛ-yāna (path of the fathers) — the path of return, leading to the moon, then back to rebirth. For those who perform rituals without knowledge. The route (Chāndogya 5.10, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 6.2): flame → day → bright fortnight → six months of the sun's northern course (uttarāyaṇa) → the year → the sun → the moon → lightning → a non-human person (amānava puruṣa) who guides them to Brahman. What 'satyena vitataḥ' means: the path is 'spread out BY truth' — truth itself is the substance of the road. The deva-yāna is not a physical route through space but a path of increasing truth-realisation. Each 'station' (flame, sun, lightning) represents a stage of consciousness-ascent. 'Āpta-kāmāḥ' — whose desires are fulfilled: the travellers on this path are 'āpta-kāma' — their desires are 'attained.' The Taittirīya (2.1.1) says of the Brahman-knower: 'āpnoti sarvān kāmān saha brahmaṇā vipaścitā' — 'they attain all desires together with the omniscient Brahman.' This doesn't mean every worldly wish is granted — it means the Self is found, and in the Self is everything one could ever desire. 'Paramaṁ nidhānam' — 'the supreme treasure': the destination is not a place but a reality — the 'supreme repository of truth,' the ultimate Real. The metaphor of 'nidhāna' (treasure) suggests that truth is not merely an attribute of reality but IS reality — and it is inexhaustibly rich, like a treasure that never runs out.

sk: बृहच्च तद्दिव्यमचिन्त्यरूपं सूक्ष्मं च तत्सूक्ष्मतरं विभाति दूरात्सुदूरे तदिहान्तिके च पश्यत्स्विहैव निहितं गुहायाम् ||
ro: bṛhat · ca · tat · divyam · acintya-rūpaṁ · sūkṣmaṁ · ca · tat · sūkṣmataragm · vibhāti · dūrāt · sudūre · tat · iha · antike · ca · paśyatsu · iha · eva · nihitaṁ · guhāyām ||
hi: बृहत् (vast / विराट) और वह (तत्) दिव्यम् (divine / दिव्य), अचिन्त्यरूपम् (of unthinkable form / अचिन्तनीय रूप वाला), सूक्ष्म (subtle / सूक्ष्म) — और सूक्ष्मतरम् (subtler than the subtle / सूक्ष्म से भी सूक्ष्मतर) विभाति (shines / प्रकाशित होता है)। दूरात् सुदूरे (far beyond the far / दूर से भी अत्यन्त दूर) — तत् (that) इह (here) अन्तिके (near / समीप) च (and also)। पश्यत्सु (among those who see / देखने वालों में) इह एव (right here) निहितम् (placed / स्थित) गुहायाम् (in the cave [of the heart])।
en: Vast (bṛhat) is that (tat), divine (divyam), of unthinkable form (acintya-rūpam), subtle (sūkṣmam) — subtler than the subtle (sūkṣmataram) It shines (vibhāti). Far beyond the far (dūrāt sudūre), yet here (iha), near (antike) — among those who see (paśyatsu), It is placed (nihitam) right here (iha eva), in the cave of the heart (guhāyām).

ws.h: अचिन्तनीय रूप वाला / सोच से परे

ws.e: in the cave / in the cave of the heart

gr:
व्याकरण: बृहत् — √बृह् (बड़ा होना) — विशेषण — 'विराट / विशाल' — ब्रह्म = सर्वव्यापक। दिव्यम् — √दिव् (प्रकाशित होना) — 'दिव्य / अलौकिक।' अचिन्त्यरूपम् — अ + चिन्त्य (√चिन्त् = सोचना + यत्) + रूप — बहुव्रीहि — 'जिसका रूप चिन्तन से परे' — 'रूपहीन' नहीं, 'रूपातीत' — मन की कल्पना-शक्ति से अधिक। सूक्ष्मम् — 'सूक्ष्म' — अत्यन्त महीन / इन्द्रिय-अगोचर। सूक्ष्मतरम् — तरप् (comparative) प्रत्यय — 'सूक्ष्म से भी अधिक सूक्ष्म' — तुलनात्मक रूप से अकथनीय सूक्ष्मता। विभाति — वि + √भा (चमकना) — 'प्रकाशमान होता है' — ब्रह्म सूक्ष्म होते हुए भी प्रकाशित — निष्क्रिय नहीं। दूरात् सुदूरे — 'दूरात्' = पञ्चमी (ablative) — 'दूर से'; 'सुदूरे' = सु (अत्यन्त) + दूर + सप्तमी — 'अत्यन्त दूर।' इह अन्तिके — 'इह' = यहाँ; 'अन्तिके' = सप्तमी — 'समीप / निकट' — विरोधाभास: दूरात् सुदूरे किन्तु इह अन्तिके। पश्यत्सु — √दृश् (पश्य्) शतृ प्रत्यय + सप्तमी बहुवचन — 'देखने वालों में।' निहितम् — नि + √धा (रखना) — भूतकृदन्त — 'रखा हुआ / स्थापित।' गुहायाम् — 'गुहा' का सप्तमी — 'गुहा/गुफा में' = हृदय-गुहा — आत्मा बाहर नहीं, हृदय के अन्तरतम कक्ष में। विरोधाभास-शृंखला: बृहत् ↔ सूक्ष्म, दिव्य ↔ गुहायाम्, दूर ↔ निकट — ब्रह्म सभी द्वन्द्वों से परे।
Eng: A chain of paradoxes: bṛhat (vast) ↔ sūkṣma (subtle), divya (transcendent) ↔ guhāyām (in the cave), dūrāt sudūre (far beyond far) ↔ iha antike (here, near). 'Acintya-rūpam' = bahuvrīhi — whose form is beyond thought (not formless but trans-formal). 'Vibhāti' (vi+√bhā) = shines forth. 'Paśyatsu' (śatṛ + saptamī) = among seers. 'Nihitam' (ni+√dhā) = placed/deposited. Brahman transcends all dualities.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — सभी विरोधाभास (paradoxes) = ब्रह्म सभी द्वन्द्वों (dualities) से परे। 'बृहत्' = सर्वव्यापक। 'सूक्ष्म' = अविभाज्य (indivisible)। 'दूरात् सुदूरे' = अज्ञानी के लिए दूर। 'इह अन्तिके' = ज्ञानी के लिए निकट — हृदय-गुहा में। ब्रह्म = अज्ञानी के लिए सुदूर, ज्ञानी के लिए सुसमीप।
advaita.en: Shankara says all paradoxes = Brahman is beyond all dualities. 'Bṛhat' = all-pervading. 'Sūkṣma' = indivisible. 'Dūrāt sudūre' = far for the ignorant. 'Iha antike' = near for the wise — in the cave of the heart. Brahman = infinitely far for the ignorant, infinitely near for the wise.
advaita.ins: Every paradox points to the same truth — Brahman can't be caught in a single category. It's vast AND subtle, far AND near, divine AND hidden in your heart. The distance is only your ignorance. The nearness is what remains when ignorance is gone. It was always right here — in the cave of the heart.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — 'बृहत्' = भगवान् विराट (immense) — सम्पूर्ण विश्व उनका शरीर। 'सूक्ष्म' = भगवान् अणु (atomic) से भी सूक्ष्म — प्रत्येक जीव में अन्तर्यामी। 'गुहायाम्' = हृदय-कमल (lotus of the heart) में — भगवान् सदा विराजमान।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says 'bṛhat' = the Lord is immense — the entire universe is His body. 'Sūkṣma' = the Lord is subtler than the atom — the inner controller in every being. 'Guhāyām' = in the lotus of the heart — the Lord always resides.
vishisht.ins: God is vaster than the universe — and subtler than an atom. Farther than the farthest star — and closer than your own heart. He lives in the cave of the heart, waiting for you to look inward. The paradox isn't a puzzle — it's an invitation.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — 'बृहत्' = विश्व-चेतना (universal consciousness)। 'सूक्ष्म' = आणविक चेतना (atomic consciousness)। 'अचिन्त्यरूप' = अतिमानसिक (supramental) = मन (mind) की सीमा से परे। चेतना सभी स्तरों (levels) पर एक साथ विद्यमान — विराट से अणु तक, दूर से निकट तक।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says 'bṛhat' = universal consciousness. 'Sūkṣma' = atomic consciousness. 'Acintya-rūpa' = supramental = beyond the mind's limit. Consciousness exists simultaneously at all levels — from the vast to the atomic, from the far to the near.
aurobindo.ins: Consciousness is simultaneously everything — vast as the universe, subtle as a quantum, far as the farthest reaches of space, near as the cave of your heart. The 'unthinkable form' isn't formless — it's a form too vast for the mind. But the seers see it — right here, right now, in the innermost cave.

dp.q: 🔍 The paradoxes of Brahman — far and near, vast and subtle
dp.a:
यह मन्त्र ब्रह्म को विरोधाभासों (paradoxes) से वर्णित करता है — उपनिषदों की सर्वत्र प्रयुक्त शैली। (1) बृहत् + सूक्ष्म: कठ (1.2.20): 'अणोरणीयान् महतो महीयान्' — 'सबसे छोटे से छोटा, सबसे बड़े से बड़ा।' ब्रह्म = एक साथ सर्वाधिक विशाल (सब कुछ समाहित करता है — 'सर्वमिदं ब्रह्म,' छान्दोग्य 3.14.1) और सर्वाधिक सूक्ष्म (अणु तक व्याप्त)। (2) दूरात् सुदूरे + इह अन्तिके: ईशा (5): 'तद्दूरे तद्वन्तिके' — ब्रह्म 'दूर' क्योंकि सभी मानसिक कोटियों से परे — कितना भी सोचो, खोजो, यात्रा करो — गलत दिशा में न मिले। किन्तु 'निकट' — 'निहितं गुहायाम्' — स्वयं आत्मा, श्वास से भी अधिक समीप। (3) दिव्य + गुहा: ब्रह्म = 'दिव्य' (सर्वोच्च सत्ता) किन्तु 'गुहा' में छिपा — सर्वाधिक अन्तरंग भीतरी कक्ष। विरोधाभास क्यों? ब्रह्म मन की वर्गीकरण-प्रणाली (बड़ा/छोटा, दूर/निकट, बाहर/भीतर) से परे — एक वर्णन भ्रामक होगा — केवल विरोधाभास — विपरीतों को एक साथ धारण करना — उस ओर संकेत कर सकता है जो दोनों से परे।

Eng: This mantra describes Brahman through paradoxes that appear throughout the Upanishads: (1) Bṛhat + sūkṣma (vast + subtle): the Kaṭha (1.2.20) says: 'aṇoḥ aṇīyān mahato mahīyān' — 'smaller than the smallest, greater than the greatest.' Brahman is simultaneously the largest thing (it encompasses everything — 'sarvam idaṁ brahma,' Chāndogya 3.14.1) and the smallest (it pervades the innermost atom — 'aṇu' in the Kaṭha). It is not one OR the other — it is BOTH. (2) Dūrāt sudūre + iha antike (far + near): the Īśā (5) captures this perfectly: 'tad dūre tad v antike' — 'It is far; It is near.' Brahman is 'far' because it transcends all mental categories — no amount of thinking, travelling, or searching will reach it if you look in the wrong direction. But it is 'near' — 'nihitaṁ guhāyām' (placed in the cave of the heart) — because it IS you, it is your innermost Self, closer than your breath. (3) Divya + guhā (divine + hidden): Brahman is 'divya' (divine/transcendent) — the most exalted reality. Yet it is 'nihitam guhāyām' — hidden/placed in the cave of the heart, the most intimate interior. Why paradoxes? Because Brahman is beyond the categories the mind uses to classify reality (big/small, far/near, inner/outer). Any single description would be misleading. Only paradoxes — holding opposites together — can point to what lies beyond both.

dp.q: 🔍 'Guhāyām' — the cave of the heart in the Upanishads
dp.a:
गुहा (cave) उपनिषदों की सर्वाधिक शक्तिशाली और बारम्बार आने वाली छवियों में से एक — हृदय का अन्तरतम कक्ष जहाँ आत्मा छिपा है। प्रमुख गुहा-प्रसंग: (1) कठ (1.2.12): 'गूहाहितं गह्वरेष्ठं पुराणम्' — 'प्राचीन, गुहा में छिपा, गहनता में स्थित।' (2) कठ (1.3.1): 'ऋतं पिबन्तौ सुकृतस्य लोके गुहां प्रविष्टौ परमे परार्धे' — 'दोनों [जीव और ब्रह्म] ऋत पीते हुए, गुहा में प्रविष्ट।' (3) तैत्तिरीय (2.1): ब्रह्म 'निहितं गुहायाम्।' (4) छान्दोग्य (8.1.1): दहर-विद्या — 'ब्रह्मपुर (शरीर) में छोटा कमल, उसमें छोटा आकाश (दहर आकाश) — वही खोजो।' गुहा क्या है? भौतिक गुफा नहीं — चेतना का अन्तरतम केन्द्र — जहाँ ध्यान में इन्द्रियों, मन, बुद्धि से भीतर जाकर शुद्ध जागरूकता पहुँचती है। शिक्षा: आत्मा मन्दिर में नहीं, पर्वत पर नहीं, सुदूर स्वर्ग में नहीं — 'निहितं गुहायाम्' — अपने अस्तित्व के अन्तरतम कक्ष में। ब्रह्म-यात्रा = अन्तर्यात्रा — अनुभव की सतह से अस्तित्व की गहराई तक।

Eng: The 'guhā' (cave) is one of the most powerful and recurring images in the Upanishads — the innermost chamber of the heart where the Self is hidden: Major guhā passages: (1) Kaṭha (1.2.12): 'guhā-hitaṁ gahvareṣṭhaṁ purāṇam' — 'The ancient one, hidden in the cave, dwelling in the abyss.' (2) Kaṭha (1.3.1): 'ṛtaṁ pibantau sukṛtasya loke guhāṁ praviṣṭau parame parārdhe' — 'The two [jīva and Brahman], drinking truth, having entered the cave, in the highest heaven.' (3) Taittirīya (2.1): Brahman is 'nihitam guhāyām' — placed in the cave. (4) Chāndogya (8.1.1): the 'dahara-vidyā' — 'In this city of Brahman [the body], there is a small lotus, a dwelling; within it, a small space (dahara ākāśa). What is within that — that should be sought.' What is the 'cave'? The guhā is not a physical cavity — it is the innermost core of consciousness, the space within the heart-centre where awareness turns upon itself. In meditation, the practitioner withdraws attention from the senses, from the mind, from the intellect, and enters the 'cave' — the space of pure awareness beyond thought. The teaching: the Self is not in a temple, on a mountaintop, or in a distant heaven. It is 'nihitaṁ guhāyām' — placed in the innermost cave of your own being. The journey to Brahman is an inward journey — from the surface of experience to the depth of being.

sk: न चक्षुषा गृह्यते नापि वाचा नान्यैर्देवैस्तपसा कर्मणा वा ज्ञानप्रसादेन विशुद्धसत्त्वस्ततस्तु तं पश्यते निष्कलं ध्यायमानः ||
ro: na · cakṣuṣā · gṛhyate · na · api · vācā · na · anyaiḥ · devaiḥ · tapasā · karmaṇā · vā · jñāna-prasādena · viśuddha-sattvaḥ · tataḥ · tu · taṁ · paśyate · niṣkalaṁ · dhyāyamānaḥ ||
hi: न चक्षुषा (not by the eye / आँख से नहीं) गृह्यते (is grasped / पकड़ा जाता), न वाचा (not by speech / वाणी से नहीं), न अन्यैः देवैः (not by other senses/gods / अन्य इन्द्रियों/देवों से नहीं), तपसा कर्मणा वा (nor by tapas or action / तप या कर्म से भी नहीं)। ज्ञानप्रसादेन (by the grace/clarity of knowledge / ज्ञान की प्रसन्नता/कृपा से) विशुद्धसत्त्वः (one whose sattva is purified / शुद्ध सत्त्व वाला) — ततः तु (then indeed) तम् (that / Him) पश्यते (sees / देखता है) निष्कलम् (the partless / निष्कल / without parts) ध्यायमानः (meditating / ध्यान करता हुआ)।
en: Not by the eye (na cakṣuṣā) is It grasped (gṛhyate), not by speech (na vācā), not by other senses/gods (na anyaiḥ devaiḥ), not by tapas or action (tapasā karmaṇā vā). By the grace/clarity of knowledge (jñāna-prasādena), one whose sattva is purified (viśuddha-sattva) — then (tataḥ tu) one sees (paśyate) that partless [Brahman] (niṣkalam), meditating (dhyāyamānaḥ).

ws.h: पकड़ा जाता है / ग्रहण किया जाता है
ज्ञान की प्रसन्नता / निर्मलता / कृपा से

gr:
व्याकरण: न चक्षुषा गृह्यते — 'चक्षुषा' = 'चक्षुस्' (नेत्र) का तृतीया — 'नेत्र द्वारा'; 'गृह्यते' = √ग्रह् (पकड़ना) कर्मणि — 'पकड़ा जाता है' — ब्रह्म इन्द्रिय-विषय नहीं। न अपि वाचा — 'वाचा' = 'वाच्' (वाणी) तृतीया — 'वाणी से भी नहीं' — शब्द ब्रह्म को व्यक्त नहीं कर सकते (तैत्तिरीय 2.9.1: 'यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते')। अन्यैः देवैः — 'देव' = इन्द्रिय-देवता (श्रोत्र, त्वक्, रसना, घ्राण) — तृतीया बहुवचन — शेष इन्द्रियाँ भी असमर्थ। तपसा कर्मणा वा — तप और कर्म भी अकेले अपर्याप्त — मुण्डक का केन्द्रीय साधन 'तप' भी यहाँ अकेला अपर्याप्त घोषित! ज्ञानप्रसादेन — ज्ञान + प्रसाद — 'प्रसाद' = √प्र-सद् (बैठना/शान्त होना) — अर्थ: (1) कृपा (grace), (2) निर्मलता/प्रसन्नता (clarity/serenity) — ज्ञान-दर्शन कृपा भी है और स्वाभाविक परिणाम भी। विशुद्धसत्त्वः — वि + शुद्ध + सत्त्व — बहुव्रीहि — 'जिसका सत्त्व (अन्तःकरण/अस्तित्व) परिशुद्ध।' पश्यते — √दृश् आत्मनेपद — 'देखता है' — आत्मनेपद = आत्म-अनुभव। निष्कलम् — निस् + कला (अंश/भाग) — 'अंशरहित / अविभाज्य' — ब्रह्म सकल (with parts) नहीं, निष्कल। ध्यायमानः — √ध्यै (ध्यान करना) शानच् — 'ध्यान करता हुआ' — दर्शन ध्यान में होता है, बौद्धिक विश्लेषण में नहीं। 'नेति नेति' संरचना: पहले 'क्या नहीं पहुँचता' (इन्द्रियाँ, वाणी, तप, कर्म), फिर 'क्या पहुँचता है' (ज्ञान-प्रसाद + शुद्ध सत्त्व + ध्यान)।
Eng: 'Na cakṣuṣā gṛhyate' = Brahman is not a sense-object. 'Vācā' = by speech (tṛtīyā of vāc). 'Jñāna-prasādena' = prasāda (√pra-sad) carries both 'grace' and 'clarity.' 'Viśuddha-sattvaḥ' = bahuvrīhi — one whose being is purified. 'Niṣkalam' = nis+kalā — partless. 'Dhyāyamānaḥ' (śānac of √dhyai) = meditating. Structure: neti neti — first what cannot reach Brahman, then what can (jñāna-prasāda + viśuddha-sattva + dhyāna).

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — 'न चक्षुषा' = इन्द्रियाँ ब्रह्म तक नहीं पहुँचतीं — ब्रह्म = इन्द्रिय-विषय (sense-object) नहीं। 'ज्ञानप्रसादेन' = ज्ञान की निर्मलता (clarity of knowledge) — बुद्धि (intellect) शान्त (serene) होने पर, मन (mind) स्वच्छ (transparent) होने पर — आत्मा स्वयं प्रकट (self-reveals)। 'निष्कलम्' = निर्गुण ब्रह्म — अंश-रहित — ध्यान (meditation) में प्रकट।
advaita.en: Shankara says 'na cakṣuṣā' = the senses cannot reach Brahman — Brahman is not a sense-object. 'Jñāna-prasādena' = the clarity of knowledge — when the intellect is serene, when the mind is transparent — the Self self-reveals. 'Niṣkalam' = nirguṇa Brahman — without parts — revealed in meditation.
advaita.ins: You can't see Brahman with your eyes, speak it with your words, or reach it with rituals and austerities. Then how? By the clarity of knowledge — when your mind becomes utterly still, utterly pure, like clear water. Then the partless Self reveals itself. Not because you grasped it — because you stopped grasping.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — 'ज्ञानप्रसादेन' = भगवत्-कृपा (God's grace) + ज्ञान (knowledge)। भगवान् = कृपा से प्राप्त — केवल स्व-प्रयत्न (self-effort) से नहीं। 'विशुद्धसत्त्वः' = शुद्ध हृदय = भक्ति (devotion) का फल। भगवान् स्वयं भक्त को दर्शन देते हैं (God reveals Himself to the devotee)।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says 'jñāna-prasādena' = God's grace + knowledge. God is attained by grace — not by self-effort alone. 'Viśuddha-sattva' = pure heart = the fruit of devotion. God Himself reveals Himself to the devotee.
vishisht.ins: Eyes can't see God. Words can't describe Him. Even tapas and ritual can't reach Him alone. Then how? By the grace of knowledge — God reveals Himself when your heart is pure. It's not your effort that brings the vision — it's His grace responding to your purity.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — इन्द्रियाँ (senses) = मानसिक चेतना (mental consciousness) — ब्रह्म तक नहीं पहुँचतीं। 'ज्ञानप्रसाद' = चेतना का उच्चतर स्तर (higher level of consciousness) — अतिमानसिक प्रज्ञा (supramental gnosis) — जो मन से परे है। 'विशुद्धसत्त्व' = अन्तर-शुद्धि (inner purification) — चेतना-रूपान्तर (consciousness-transformation) का पूर्वापेक्ष (prerequisite)।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says senses = mental consciousness — cannot reach Brahman. 'Jñāna-prasāda' = a higher level of consciousness — supramental gnosis — beyond the mind. 'Viśuddha-sattva' = inner purification — the prerequisite for consciousness-transformation.
aurobindo.ins: The senses are instruments of the mind — they can't reach what is beyond the mind. Neither can tapas or action alone. What reaches Brahman is a higher consciousness — the gnosis that descends when the inner being is purified. It's not effort that produces the vision — it's the clearing of obstacles so that the light, which is always there, can enter.

dp.q: 🔍 'Jñāna-prasāda' — the debate between effort and grace
dp.a:
'ज्ञानप्रसाद' शब्द मुण्डक के सर्वाधिक चर्चित पदों में है — स्व-प्रयत्न और दिव्य कृपा के चिरन्तन तनाव के मध्य। प्रयत्न-पक्ष: मन्त्र 3.2.5 ने चार साधन बताए — सत्य, तप, सम्यग्ज्ञान, ब्रह्मचर्य — स्पष्टतः मानवीय प्रयत्न। साधक को 'विशुद्धसत्त्व' (शुद्ध अन्तःकरण) भी चाहिए — जो निरन्तर साधना से आता है। कृपा-पक्ष: यही मन्त्र (3.2.8) कहता है कि प्रयत्न का कोई भी साधन — इन्द्रियाँ, वाणी, तप, कर्म — ब्रह्म को 'पकड़' नहीं सकता। केवल 'ज्ञानप्रसाद' से। 'प्रसाद' = कृपा/दान/शान्ति — कुछ प्राप्त होने का सूचक। कठ समानान्तर (1.2.23): 'यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्यः' — 'जिसे आत्मा चुनता है, उसे प्राप्त।' आत्मा चुनता है और प्रकट करता है — साधक पकड़ता नहीं। समाधान: दोनों आवश्यक: (1) स्व-प्रयत्न (चतुर्विध साधना) = भूमि-तैयारी — शुद्धि, बाधा-निवारण, परिस्थिति-निर्माण। (2) कृपा/निर्मलता (प्रसाद) = दर्शन का क्षण — परिस्थितियाँ अनुकूल होने पर अवतरित, किन्तु निर्माण-योग्य नहीं। स्वच्छ कमरे में दीपक — कमरा साफ करना (प्रयत्न), प्रकाश स्वयं जलता है (कृपा)।

Eng: The term 'jñāna-prasāda' is one of the most debated in the Muṇḍaka — it sits at the intersection of the age-old tension between self-effort and divine grace: The effort side: mantra 3.2.5 just prescribed FOUR sādhanas — satya, tapas, samyag-jñāna, brahmacarya. These are clearly human efforts — things the aspirant does. And the aspirant must be 'viśuddha-sattva' (purified in being) — which requires sustained practice. The grace side: this mantra (3.2.8) says that NONE of the instruments of effort — senses, speech, tapas, karma — can 'grasp' Brahman. Only 'jñāna-prasāda' can. The word 'prasāda' means grace/gift/serenity — suggesting something received, not produced. The Kaṭha parallel (1.2.23) makes the grace dimension explicit: 'yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyaḥ' — 'He whom the Self CHOOSES, by him is the Self attained — to him the Self reveals Its own form.' The Self chooses and reveals — the aspirant does not seize it. The resolution: most commentators agree that BOTH are necessary: (1) Self-effort (the fourfold sādhana) prepares the ground — it purifies the sattva, removes obstacles, creates the conditions. (2) Grace/clarity (prasāda) is the actual moment of seeing — it descends when conditions are right, but it cannot be manufactured. It is like lighting a lamp in a clean room — you must clean the room (effort), but the light illumines on its own (grace). The practical implication: do the work (satya, tapas, jñāna, brahmacarya) — but don't imagine that the work itself produces the result. The result is a revelation — the Self reveals itself when you are ready. Your job is to be ready.

dp.q: 🔍 'Niṣkalam' — the partless Brahman
dp.a:
'निष्कलम्' (अंशरहित / अविभाज्य) शब्द ब्रह्म के स्वरूप को चरम दर्शन में वर्णित करता है। 'अंशरहित' का अर्थ: (1) दैशिक अंश नहीं: ब्रह्म में ऊपर-नीचे, दायाँ-बायाँ, भीतर-बाहर नहीं — स्थान-विभाज्य नहीं। (2) कालिक अंश नहीं: आदि, मध्य, अन्त नहीं — काल-विभाज्य नहीं। (3) गुणात्मक अंश नहीं: विभिन्न गुणों या विशेषताओं का संयोजन नहीं — सरल, अविभेदित एकत्व। निष्कल बनाम सकल: (अ) सकल ब्रह्म = जगत् में प्रकट ब्रह्म — नाम, रूप, गुण सहित — माया/अविद्या के चश्मे से। (ब) निष्कल ब्रह्म = स्वरूपतः ब्रह्म — सभी विभेदों से परे — परम सत्ता। ध्यान-अनुभव: 'निष्कलं ध्यायमानः' — गहन ध्यान में सभी भेद विलीन — ज्ञाता-ज्ञेय, आत्मा-जगत्, विषय-विषयी — शेष रहता है अविभाज्य, अखण्ड बोध — 'निष्कल' — यह अभाव (शून्य) नहीं, उपस्थिति (सब एकीकृत)। श्वेताश्वतर (6.19): 'निष्कलं निष्क्रियं शान्तम् — अवद्यं निरञ्जनम्' — अंशरहित, क्रियारहित, शान्त, दोषरहित, कलंकरहित।

Eng: The word 'niṣkalam' (partless / without divisions) describes the nature of Brahman as seen in the ultimate vision: What does 'partless' mean? (1) No spatial parts: Brahman doesn't have a top and a bottom, a left and a right, an inside and an outside. It cannot be divided in space. (2) No temporal parts: Brahman doesn't have a beginning, a middle, and an end. It cannot be divided in time. (3) No qualitative parts: Brahman is not composed of different qualities or attributes that could be separated. It is a simple, undifferentiated unity. Niṣkala vs. sakala: the Upanishads distinguish between: (a) Sakala Brahman (Brahman with parts) — Brahman as manifested in the world, with names, forms, and qualities. This is Brahman as seen through the lens of māyā/avidyā. (b) Niṣkala Brahman (Brahman without parts) — Brahman as it is in itself, beyond all differentiation. This is the ultimate reality. The meditative experience: 'niṣkalaṁ dhyāyamānaḥ' — 'meditating on the partless.' In deep meditation, all distinctions dissolve — subject and object, knower and known, self and world. What remains is a partless, undivided awareness — 'niṣkala.' This is not an absence (nothing left) but a presence (everything unified). The Śvetāśvatara (6.19): 'niṣkalaṁ niṣkriyaṁ śāntam — avadyaṁ nirañjanam' — 'Partless, actionless, peaceful — faultless, stainless.' The niṣkala Brahman is also niṣkriya (actionless), śānta (peaceful), niravadya (faultless), and nirañjana (stainless) — a cluster of negative descriptions pointing to a reality beyond all limitation.

sk: एषोऽणुरात्मा चेतसा वेदितव्यो यस्मिन्प्राणः पञ्चधा संविवेश चित्तं प्रजानां सर्वमोतं प्रोतं यस्मिन्विशुद्धे विभवत्येष आत्मा ||
ro: eṣaḥ · aṇuḥ · ātmā · cetasā · veditavyaḥ · yasmin · prāṇaḥ · pañcadhā · saṁviveśa · cittaṁ · prajānāṁ · sarvam · otaṁ · protaṁ · yasmin · viśuddhe · vibhavati · eṣaḥ · ātmā ||
hi: यह (एषः) अणु (subtle / atomic / सूक्ष्म) आत्मा (Self) चेतसा (by the mind/consciousness / चित्त/बुद्धि से) वेदितव्यः (is to be known / जानने योग्य) है — जिसमें (यस्मिन्) प्राण पञ्चधा (fivefold / पाँच प्रकार से) संविवेश (has entered / प्रविष्ट हुआ है)। प्रजानाम् (of beings / प्राणियों का) सर्वम् चित्तम् (all mind/consciousness) ओतं प्रोतम् (woven warp and weft / ताने-बाने की तरह बुना हुआ) — जिसमें (यस्मिन्) विशुद्धे (when purified / शुद्ध होने पर) विभवति (manifests / प्रकट होता है) यह (एषः) आत्मा (Self)।
en: This subtle (aṇu) Self (ātmā) is to be known (veditavyaḥ) by the mind/consciousness (cetasā) — in which (yasmin) prāṇa has entered (saṁviveśa) fivefold (pañcadhā). The mind/consciousness (citta) of all beings (prajānām) is woven warp and weft (otaṁ protam) [in the Self] — when that [mind] is purified (viśuddhe), this Self (eṣa ātmā) manifests (vibhavati).

ws.e: is to be known / should be known
woven in the warp / lengthwise threads
woven in the weft / crosswise threads

ws.h: शुद्ध होने पर / परिशुद्ध होने पर
प्रकट होता है / प्रकाशित होता है

gr:
