व्याकरण: एषः अणुः आत्मा — 'अणुः' = अत्यन्त सूक्ष्म — विशेषण — आत्मा = स्थूल नहीं, इन्द्रिय-ग्राह्य नहीं। चेतसा — 'चेतस्' (चित्त/मन) तृतीया — 'चित्त द्वारा' — पूर्व मन्त्र 'न चक्षुषा' (इन्द्रियों से नहीं) के बाद यहाँ साधन बताया — 'चेतस्' (शुद्ध चित्त)। वेदितव्यः — √विद् (जानना) + तव्यत् प्रत्यय — विधि-विशेषण — 'जानना चाहिए / ज्ञातव्य।' यस्मिन् — सप्तमी — 'जिसमें।' पञ्चधा — अव्यय — 'पाँच प्रकार से' — पञ्च प्राण: प्राण, अपान, व्यान, उदान, समान। संविवेश — सम् + वि + √विश् (प्रवेश करना) — लिट् लकार — 'प्रविष्ट हो गया है' — प्राण आत्मा में कार्यरत, आत्मा प्राण का आधार। चित्तम् प्रजानाम् — 'चित्तम्' = मन/चेतना; 'प्रजानाम्' = षष्ठी बहुवचन — 'प्राणियों का।' ओतम् प्रोतम् — √वे (बुनना — ताना) = 'ओत' + √प्र-वे (बुनना — बाना) = 'प्रोत' — वस्त्र-बुनाई रूपक — आत्मा = चेतना का ताना-बाना — कपड़े में तन्तु जैसे — अलग नहीं किया जा सकता। यस्मिन् विशुद्धे — 'विशुद्धे' = सप्तमी, सति सप्तमी (locative absolute) — 'जब वह (चित्त) शुद्ध हो' — शर्त। विभवति — वि + √भू (होना/प्रकट होना) — 'प्रकट होता है / प्रभावशाली होता है' — आत्मा सदा है, शुद्धि पर प्रकट।
Eng: 'Cetasā veditavyaḥ' (tavyat pratyaya of √vid) = to be known by the purified mind. 'Pañcadhā saṁviveśa' (liṭ of sam+vi+√viś) = prāṇa has entered fivefold. 'Otaṁ protam' — from √ve (weave warp) and pra+√ve (weave weft) — the Self is woven through consciousness as threads through cloth. 'Viśuddhe' = sati saptamī (locative absolute) — 'when purified.' 'Vibhavati' (vi+√bhū) = manifests.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — 'चेतसा वेदितव्यः' = शुद्ध बुद्धि (purified intellect) से ज्ञेय। 'ओतं प्रोतम्' = आत्मा = सम्पूर्ण चेतना (all consciousness) का अधिष्ठान (substratum) — ताना-बाना। 'विशुद्धे विभवति' = चित्त-शुद्धि (citta-purification) से आत्मा प्रकट — आत्मा सदा विद्यमान (always present) — किन्तु अशुद्धि (impurity) आवरण (covering) है।
advaita.en: Shankara says 'cetasā veditavyaḥ' = to be known by the purified intellect. 'Otaṁ protam' = the Self = the substratum of all consciousness — warp and weft. 'Viśuddhe vibhavati' = through citta-purification, the Self manifests — the Self is always present but impurity is the covering.
advaita.ins: The Self is woven through your entire consciousness — every thought, every breath, every moment. Like thread in cloth, you can't separate it out. You can only see it by purifying the mind. When the mind is clear — the Self that was always there finally shows itself.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — 'अणुः आत्मा' = जीवात्मा = अणु-स्वरूप (atomic in nature) — भगवान् में अंश (part/mode of God)। 'ओतं प्रोतम्' = भगवान् = सम्पूर्ण चेतना में व्याप्त — अन्तर्यामी। 'विशुद्धे विभवति' = भक्ति-शुद्ध हृदय (devotion-purified heart) में भगवान् प्रकट।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says 'aṇuḥ ātmā' = the individual Self = atomic in nature — a part/mode of God. 'Otaṁ protam' = God pervades all consciousness — as the inner controller. 'Viśuddhe vibhavati' = God manifests in the devotion-purified heart.
vishisht.ins: God is woven through the consciousness of every being — warp and weft, inseparable from awareness itself. He's in every breath, every thought. Purify your heart through devotion, and He manifests — not from outside but from within, where He's always been.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — 'ओतं प्रोतम्' = चेतना (consciousness) = आत्मा (Self) का ताना-बाना। मन, प्राण, शरीर — सब चेतना से बुने हुए। 'विशुद्धे विभवति' = चेतना-शुद्धि (consciousness-purification) से आत्मा प्रकट — योग = चेतना-शुद्धि की प्रक्रिया।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says 'otaṁ protam' = consciousness = the warp and weft of the Self. Mind, prāṇa, body — all woven from consciousness. 'Viśuddhe vibhavati' = through consciousness-purification, the Self manifests — yoga = the process of consciousness-purification.
aurobindo.ins: Consciousness is not contained in the body — the body is contained in consciousness. The Self is woven through all awareness — mind, life, body — as thread through cloth. Purify consciousness, and the Self that was always the fabric of your being reveals itself. The thread was never hidden — your eyes were clouded.

dp.q: 🔍 'Otaṁ protam' — the weaving metaphor for Self and consciousness
dp.a:
'ओतं प्रोतम्' (ताने-बाने में बुना हुआ) उपनिषदों के सर्वाधिक ज्वलन्त और दार्शनिक रूप से महत्त्वपूर्ण रूपकों में से एक है। रूपक: बुनाई में ताना (ota/warp) = करघे पर लम्बवत् तने तन्तु, बाना (prota/weft) = उनमें से गुज़रने वाले अनुप्रस्थ तन्तु। दोनों मिलकर = वस्त्र। मुण्डक कहता है: आत्मा = चेतना में ताने-बाने की भाँति — दोनों दिशाओं में, हर बिन्दु पर, अविच्छेद्य। बृहदारण्यक (3.8.7-8): गार्गी का प्रश्न — 'आकाश स्वयं किसमें ओत-प्रोत है?' याज्ञवल्क्य: 'अक्षर (अविनाशी) में, हे गार्गी — अक्षर ही आकाश का भी ताना-बाना।' शिक्षा: (1) व्यापकता: कपड़े में कोई भाग तन्तु-रहित नहीं — चेतना में कोई क्षण आत्मा-रहित नहीं। (2) घनिष्ठता: आत्मा चेतना 'में' नहीं जैसे पत्थर कटोरे में — आत्मा चेतना है — उसी पदार्थ से। (3) अविच्छेद्यता: तन्तु हटाओ तो कपड़ा नष्ट — आत्मा हटाओ तो चेतना नष्ट। (4) गुप्तता: बने कपड़े में तन्तु तुरन्त दिखते नहीं — आप बुनावट, रंग, डिज़ाइन देखते हैं — वैसे आत्मा चेतना में गुप्त — विद्यमान किन्तु सतही दृष्टि को अदृश्य।

Eng: The image of 'otaṁ protam' (woven warp and weft) is one of the most vivid and philosophically significant metaphors in the Upanishads: The metaphor: in weaving, the warp (ota) consists of the lengthwise threads stretched on the loom, and the weft (prota) consists of the crosswise threads woven through them. Together, they create the fabric. The Muṇḍaka says: the Self is woven through consciousness like thread through cloth — in BOTH directions, at every point, inseparable from the fabric. The Bṛhadāraṇyaka version (3.8.7-8): Gārgī asks Yājñavalkya one of the most searching questions in all Upanishadic dialogue: 'In what is space itself woven, warp and weft?' Yājñavalkya answers: 'In the akṣara (the Imperishable), O Gārgī — that is the warp and weft of space itself.' What the metaphor teaches: (1) Pervasiveness: you cannot find a part of the cloth that is without thread. Similarly, you cannot find a moment of consciousness without the Self. (2) Intimacy: the Self is not 'in' consciousness the way a stone is in a bowl — it IS consciousness, the very substance from which awareness is made. (3) Inseparability: you cannot remove the thread without destroying the cloth. Similarly, the Self cannot be separated from consciousness — it IS what consciousness is. (4) Hiddenness: thread in a finished cloth is not immediately visible as individual threads — you see the pattern, the colour, the design, but not the individual threads. Similarly, the Self is 'hidden' in consciousness — present but not immediately obvious.

dp.q: 🔍 'Yasmin viśuddhe vibhavati' — purification as the key to Self-realisation
dp.a:
'यस्मिन् विशुद्धे विभवत्येष आत्मा' ('जब वह [चित्त] शुद्ध हो, तब यह आत्मा प्रकट होता है') — मुण्डक का अन्तिम व्यावहारिक निर्देश। तर्क: (1) आत्मा सदा विद्यमान — 'ओतं प्रोतम्' — कभी अनुपस्थित नहीं, कभी दूर नहीं, कभी छिपा नहीं। (2) आत्मा दिखता नहीं क्योंकि चित्त अशुद्ध — काम, द्वेष, मोह, मद, अन्य दोषों से आच्छादित। (3) जब चित्त विशुद्ध (thoroughly purified), आत्मा 'विभवति' (manifests) — बाहर से नहीं आता, आवरण हटता है। उपमा: धूलभरा दर्पण प्रतिबिम्बित नहीं करता — दर्पण ठीक, प्रतिबिम्ब-क्षमता अक्षुण्ण — समस्या धूल — धूल साफ़ करो, दर्पण स्वतः प्रतिबिम्बित करे। शुद्धि कैसे? मुण्डक ने उत्तरोत्तर बताया: (1) चतुर्विध साधना (3.2.5): सत्य, तप, सम्यग्ज्ञान, ब्रह्मचर्य। (2) ज्ञान-कृपा (3.2.8): ज्ञानप्रसाद। (3) निष्कल-ध्यान (3.2.8): ध्यायमानः निष्कलम्। तीनों मिलकर — नैतिक शुद्धि, बौद्धिक निर्मलता, ध्यान-समाधि — चित्त शुद्ध, आत्मा प्रकट। योग सूत्र समानान्तर (1.2-3): 'योगश्चित्तवृत्तिनिरोधः' → 'तदा द्रष्टुः स्वरूपेऽवस्थानम्' — वृत्ति-निरोध = चित्तशुद्धि → द्रष्टा स्वरूप में स्थित = आत्मप्रकटन। वही शिक्षा, वही तर्क।

Eng: The phrase 'yasmin viśuddhe vibhavati eṣa ātmā' ('when that [mind] is purified, this Self manifests') gives the Muṇḍaka's final practical instruction: The logic: (1) The Self is already present — it is 'otaṁ protam' (woven through all consciousness). It was never absent, never distant, never hidden. (2) The Self is not perceived because the citta (mind/consciousness) is aśuddha (impure) — clouded by desire, aversion, delusion, pride, and other doṣas (faults). (3) When the citta becomes viśuddha (thoroughly purified), the Self 'vibhavati' (manifests) — not because it arrives from elsewhere but because the covering is removed. The analogy: a mirror covered with dust doesn't reflect. The mirror is fine; the reflective surface is intact. The problem is the dust. Clean the dust, and the mirror reflects perfectly. Similarly, the Self is always 'reflecting' — but the impurities of the mind prevent the reflection from being seen. How to purify? The Muṇḍaka has answered this progressively: (1) The fourfold sādhana (3.2.5): satya, tapas, samyag-jñāna, brahmacarya. (2) The grace of knowledge (3.2.8): jñāna-prasāda. (3) Meditation on the partless (3.2.8): dhyāyamānaḥ niṣkalam. All three work together — ethical practice, intellectual clarity, and meditative absorption — to purify the citta and allow the ever-present Self to shine forth. The Yoga Sūtra parallel (1.2-3): Patañjali's formulation is virtually identical: 'yogaś citta-vṛtti-nirodhaḥ' (yoga = the cessation of mental fluctuations). 'Tadā draṣṭuḥ svarūpe'vasthānam' (then the seer abides in its own nature). When the mental fluctuations (vṛttis) cease — i.e., when the citta is purified — the seer (draṣṭṛ = the witness-Self) 'abides in its own form.' The same teaching, the same logic.

sk: यं यं लोकं मनसा संविभाति विशुद्धसत्त्वः कामयते यांश्च कामान् तं तं लोकं जयते तांश्च कामांस्तस्मादात्मज्ञं ह्यर्चयेद्भूतिकामः ||
ro: yaṁ · yaṁ · lokaṁ · manasā · saṁvibhāti · viśuddha-sattvaḥ · kāmayate · yāṁś · ca · kāmān · taṁ · taṁ · lokaṁ · jayate · tāṁś · ca · kāmān · tasmāt · ātma-jñaṁ · hi · arcayet · bhūti-kāmaḥ ||
en: Whatever world (yaṁ yaṁ lokam) [the knower] of purified sattva (viśuddha-sattva) envisions (saṁvibhāti) with the mind (manasā), and whatever desires (yāṁś ca kāmān) he desires (kāmayate) — that world (taṁ taṁ lokam) he wins (jayate), and those desires (tāṁś ca kāmān) [he fulfils]. Therefore (tasmāt), one who desires prosperity (bhūti-kāma) should worship (arcayet) the knower of the Self (ātma-jñam).
hi: जिस-जिस (यं-यं) लोक (world) को विशुद्धसत्त्व (purified being / शुद्ध सत्त्व वाला) मनसा (by mind / मन से) संविभाति (envisions / contemplates) और जिन-जिन कामों (desires) को कामयते (desires / चाहता है) — उन-उन लोकों को जयते (wins / जीत लेता है), और उन कामों को [पूर्ण करता है]। इसलिए (तस्मात्) भूतिकामः (one who desires prosperity / ऐश्वर्य चाहने वाला) आत्मज्ञम् (the knower of the Self / आत्मज्ञानी) को अर्चयेत् (should worship / should honour / पूजे)।

ws.e: by the mind / with the mind

ws.h: देखता है / ध्यान में प्रकाशित करता है
शुद्ध सत्त्व वाला / शुद्ध अन्तःकरण वाला

gr:
व्याकरण: यं यम् — 'यत्' सर्वनाम का द्वितीया एकवचन — द्विरुक्ति (reduplication) = 'जो-जो / जिस-जिस भी' — असीमित शक्ति का संकेत। लोकम् — द्वितीया — कर्म कारक। मनसा — 'मनस्' तृतीया — 'मन द्वारा' — संकल्प-शक्ति। संविभाति — सम् + वि + √भा (चमकना/प्रकाशित होना) — 'ध्यान में प्रकाशित करता है / मन से देखता है' — साधारण कल्पना नहीं, शुद्ध चेतना का सृजनात्मक प्रकाश। विशुद्धसत्त्वः — बहुव्रीहि — 'जिसका सत्त्व परिशुद्ध' — प्रथमा — कर्ता। कामयते — √कम् आत्मनेपद — 'चाहता है।' यान् च कामान् — 'यत्' + 'काम' द्वितीया बहुवचन — 'और जो-जो कामनाएँ।' तं तम् लोकम् जयते — 'तत्' + 'लोक' — 'उस-उस लोक को जीतता है'; 'जयते' = √जि आत्मनेपद। तस्मात् — हेत्वर्थक — 'इसलिए' — निष्कर्ष। आत्मज्ञम् — आत्मन् + ज्ञ (√ज्ञा) — तत्पुरुष — द्वितीया — 'आत्मज्ञानी को' — कर्म कारक। अर्चयेत् — √अर्च् (पूजा करना) णिच् + विधिलिङ् (optative) — 'पूजा करनी चाहिए' — विधि-वाक्य। भूतिकामः — भूति (ऐश्वर्य/समृद्धि) + काम — बहुव्रीहि — 'जो ऐश्वर्य चाहता है' — सांसारिक श्रोता को सम्बोधन। मन्त्र दो दावे करता है: (1) शुद्ध ज्ञानी का मन सृजनशील, (2) सांसारिक व्यक्ति को भी आत्मज्ञानी की पूजा करनी चाहिए।
Eng: 'Yaṁ yam' = reduplication for 'whichever.' 'Saṁvibhāti' (sam+vi+√bhā) = envisions with creative luminosity. 'Jayate' (√ji, ātmanepada) = wins/conquers. 'Arcayet' (√arc, ṇic + vidhiliṅ) = optative — 'should worship.' 'Bhūti-kāmaḥ' = bahuvrīhi — one who desires prosperity. 'Ātma-jñam' = tatpuruṣa — the Self-knower. Two claims: (1) the purified knower's mind is creative, (2) even worldly people should honour the ātma-jña.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — 'विशुद्धसत्त्वः' = ज्ञानी का मन (mind) = सत्य (truth) के अनुरूप — अतः उसका संकल्प (will) फलित होता है। 'आत्मज्ञं अर्चयेत्' = आत्मज्ञानी = सर्वोच्च (supreme) — मोक्ष न चाहने वाले भी उनका आदर करें — क्योंकि उनका सान्निध्य (proximity) = कल्याणकारी।
advaita.en: Shankara says 'viśuddha-sattva' = the knower's mind = aligned with truth — hence their will is effective. 'Ātma-jñaṁ arcayet' = the Self-knower = supreme — even those who don't seek mokṣa should honour them — because their proximity is beneficial.
advaita.ins: The sage's mind is aligned with reality — what they envision, happens. Not magic — alignment. Truth itself supports their will. Even if you only want worldly success, honour the sage. Their presence transforms you — not because of any ritual, but because of what they are.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — 'विशुद्धसत्त्वः' = भगवद्-भक्त (God-devotee) — जिसका हृदय शुद्ध — उसकी प्रार्थना (prayer) फलित (fruitful)। 'आत्मज्ञं अर्चयेत्' = भक्त-सेवा (serving the devotee) = भगवद्-सेवा (serving God) — क्योंकि भक्त = भगवान् का प्रतिनिधि (representative of God)।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says 'viśuddha-sattva' = the God-devotee — whose heart is pure — their prayer is fruitful. 'Ātma-jñaṁ arcayet' = serving the devotee = serving God — because the devotee is God's representative.
vishisht.ins: The pure devotee's prayers are answered — not because of magical powers but because God honours the devotee's will. If you want prosperity, serve the devotee. Serving God's beloved is serving God Himself.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — 'संविभाति' = शुद्ध चेतना (purified consciousness) = सृजनात्मक (creative)। चेतना = शक्ति (force) — शुद्ध चेतना का संकल्प (will) = सत्य-शक्ति (truth-force) — जो वास्तविकता (reality) को आकार देती है। 'आत्मज्ञं अर्चयेत्' = चेतना-विकास (consciousness-evolution) में आत्मज्ञानी = अग्रदूत (pioneer)।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says 'saṁvibhāti' = purified consciousness = creative. Consciousness = force — purified consciousness's will = truth-force — which shapes reality. 'Ātma-jñaṁ arcayet' = in consciousness-evolution, the Self-knower = the pioneer.
aurobindo.ins: Purified consciousness is creative. What the sage envisions becomes real — not through desire but through truth-force. If you want prosperity, approach the one whose consciousness is purified — the one who knows the Self. Their very presence realigns your consciousness with truth.

dp.q: 🔍 The creative power of the purified mind (saṅkalpa-śakti)
dp.a:
यह मन्त्र शुद्ध चित्त वाले ज्ञानी को सृजनात्मक शक्ति (saṅkalpa-śakti) प्रदान करता है — 'जो-जो लोक ध्यान में देखे, जीतता है; जो-जो कामना करे, पूर्ण हो।' यह शक्ति क्या है? (1) मनोकामना-पूर्ति / जादू नहीं: मन्त्र अलौकिक शक्तियों का नहीं, सत्य (truth/reality) के साथ तालमेल का वर्णन करता है — जब मन विशुद्ध हो, उसकी धारणाएँ और संकल्प यथार्थ के अनुकूल — ऐसे मन से जन्मा कर्म स्वाभाविक सफल। (2) संकल्प-शक्ति: छान्दोग्य (7.4.1) — 'संकल्पो वै मनः' — 'संकल्प ही मन का सार।' शुद्ध मन = अविकृत संकल्प = प्रभावी। (3) ऋत-अनुकूलता: शुद्ध मन ऋत (विश्व-व्यवस्था) के अनुकूल — उसकी कामनाएँ स्वार्थी या यादृच्छिक नहीं, विश्व-प्रवाह के सहज — धारा के साथ तैरना, विरुद्ध नहीं। 'भूतिकामाः' के लिए व्यावहारिक शिक्षा: सांसारिक समृद्धि भी चाहो तो सन्त ही सर्वश्रेष्ठ आश्रय — अलौकिक वरदान नहीं, शुद्ध चेतना का सान्निध्य आपकी चेतना रूपान्तरित करता है — सन्त की सत्यनिष्ठा, निर्मलता, यथार्थ-अनुकूलता संक्रामक।

Eng: This mantra ascribes creative power to the purified mind of the Self-knower — 'whatever world he envisions, he wins; whatever he desires, he fulfils': What is this power? (1) Not magical thinking: the mantra doesn't describe wish-fulfilment or supernatural powers (though later traditions read it this way). It describes the natural consequence of a mind aligned with satya (truth/reality). When the mind is viśuddha (purified), its perceptions and intentions are in harmony with the way things actually are — and actions born from such a mind naturally succeed. (2) Saṅkalpa-śakti (the power of resolve): in the Chāndogya (7.4.1), Sanatkumāra teaches: 'saṅkalpo vai manaḥ' — 'resolve is the essence of mind.' The mind's deepest power is its capacity to intend — to direct consciousness toward a goal. When the mind is pure, this power is undistorted and effective. (3) Alignment with ṛta: the Vedic concept of ṛta (cosmic order/truth) means that reality has an inherent order. A purified mind is aligned with this order — its desires are not random or selfish but in harmony with the cosmic flow. Such desires naturally fulfil themselves because they swim with the current of reality, not against it. The practical teaching for 'bhūti-kāmāḥ': even if you seek worldly prosperity, the sage is your best resource — not because the sage can magically grant wishes, but because proximity to a purified consciousness transforms your own consciousness. The sage's clarity, truthfulness, and alignment with reality become contagious.

dp.q: 🔍 'Ātma-jñaṁ arcayet' — why worship the Self-knower?
dp.a:
'आत्मज्ञं अर्चयेत्' (आत्मज्ञानी की पूजा करो) मुण्डक का अन्तिम सामाजिक उपदेश है। पदक्रम का उलटाव: वैदिक समाज में सर्वाधिक सम्मानित = राजा (क्षत्रिय) और याज्ञिक ब्राह्मण। मुण्डक आत्मज्ञ — आत्मा के ज्ञाता — को सबसे ऊपर रखता है — चाहे वे पुरोहित न हों, यज्ञ न करें, कोई सामाजिक पद न हो — उनकी पूजा होनी चाहिए। आध्यात्मिक अधिकार का सामाजिक अधिकार पर विजय। पूजा क्यों? (1) रूपान्तरकारी सान्निध्य: सन्त का सान्निध्य उनके आसपास के लोगों को शुद्ध करता है — अग्नि जैसे — निकट का सब गरम। (2) अस्तित्व द्वारा शिक्षा: सन्त शब्दों से नहीं (न अतिवादी — 3.1.4), अस्तित्व से सिखाता है — आत्मक्रीडा और आत्मरति ही शिक्षा। (3) सांसारिक और आध्यात्मिक का सेतु: 'भूतिकामाः' (समृद्धि-इच्छुक) सन्त के पास सांसारिक लाभ हेतु आएँ, आध्यात्मिक उन्नति ले जाएँ। गुरु-भक्ति परम्परा: तैत्तिरीय (1.11.2): 'आचार्यदेवो भव।' कठ (1.2.8-9): नचिकेता-यम। मुण्डक (1.2.12): 'तद्विज्ञानार्थं स गुरुमेवाभिगच्छेत्।' अन्तिम मन्त्र वृत्त पूर्ण करता है — गुरु के पास गया शिष्य अन्ततः आत्मज्ञ बने — दूसरों द्वारा पूज्य।

Eng: The instruction 'ātma-jñaṁ arcayet' (worship the knower of the Self) is the Muṇḍaka's closing social teaching: The reversal of hierarchy: in Vedic society, the most honoured figures were kings (kṣatriyas) and priests (brāhmaṇas who perform rituals). The Muṇḍaka places the ātma-jña — the sage who knows the Self — above both. The Self-knower may not be a priest, may not perform rituals, may not hold any social rank — but they are to be worshipped. This is a radical statement of spiritual over social authority. Why worship the sage? (1) Transformative presence: the sage's presence purifies those around them — like a fire that warms everything nearby. Contact with a Self-knower accelerates the seeker's own development. (2) Teaching by being: the sage teaches not primarily through words (na ativādī — 3.1.4) but through being. Their state of ātma-krīḍa (playing in the Self) and ātma-rati (delighting in the Self) is itself the teaching. (3) The bridge for the worldly: for 'bhūti-kāmāḥ' (those who desire prosperity), the sage is the bridge between worldly aspiration and spiritual transformation. Even if one comes to the sage for worldly blessings, one receives spiritual upliftment. The Upanishadic tradition of guru-bhakti: this instruction connects to the guru-śiṣya (teacher-student) tradition that runs through all the Upanishads. The Taittirīya (1.11.2): 'ācārya-devo bhava' — let the teacher be your god. The Kaṭha (1.2.8-9): Nachiketa approaches Yama as a student approaches a teacher. The Muṇḍaka (1.2.12): 'tad-vijñānārthaṁ sa gurum evābhigacchet' — 'for the knowledge of That, one should approach a guru.' The closing verse of the Muṇḍaka now completes the circle — the student who approaches the guru ultimately becomes an ātma-jña worthy of worship by others.

sk: स वेदैतत्परमं ब्रह्म धाम यत्र विश्वं निहितं भाति शुभ्रम् उपासते पुरुषं ये ह्यकामास्ते शुक्रमेतदतिवर्तन्ति धीराः ||
ro: saḥ · veda · etat · paramaṁ · brahma · dhāma · yatra · viśvaṁ · nihitaṁ · bhāti · śubhram · upāsate · puruṣaṁ · ye · hi · akāmāḥ · te · śukram · etat · ativartanti · dhīrāḥ ||
hi: वह (सः) जानता है (वेद) इस (एतत्) परम ब्रह्म-धाम (supreme abode of Brahman / ब्रह्म के परम निवास) को — जहाँ (यत्र) विश्व (the universe) निहितम् (is placed / स्थित) है, भाति (shines / प्रकाशित होता है) शुभ्रम् (resplendent / शुद्ध)। जो (ये) अकामाः (desireless / निष्काम) पुरुष (the Person) को उपासते (worship / उपासना करते हैं) — वे (ते) धीराः (the wise / steady / धीर) शुक्रम् एतत् (this seed / luminous principle / बीज-तत्त्व) अतिवर्तन्ति (transcend / pass beyond / अतिक्रमण करते हैं)।
en: He knows (veda) this (etat) supreme abode of Brahman (paramaṁ brahma-dhāma), where (yatra) the universe (viśvam) is placed (nihitam), shining (bhāti) resplendent (śubhram). Those (ye) who are desireless (akāmāḥ) [and] worship (upāsate) the Person (puruṣam) — they (te), the wise (dhīrāḥ), transcend (ativartanti) this luminous seed (śukram etat).

ws.h: उपासना करते हैं / ध्यान करते हैं
अतिक्रमण करते हैं / पार कर जाते हैं

ws.e: the wise / the steady / the resolute

gr:
व्याकरण: सः वेद — 'सः' = प्रथमा सर्वनाम — 'वह'; 'वेद' = √विद् (जानना) लिट् लकार एकवचन — 'जानता है' — वर्तमान अर्थ में प्रयुक्त (लिट् कभी-कभी वर्तमान अर्थ देता है — विशेषकर 'वेद' में)। परमं ब्रह्मधाम — 'परमम्' = सर्वोच्च; 'ब्रह्मधाम' = ब्रह्म + धामन् (√धा = रखना / धारण करना) — 'ब्रह्म का निवास / ब्रह्म का तेज / ब्रह्म का स्थान' — स्थान नहीं, चेतना-अवस्था। यत्र — अव्यय — 'जहाँ।' विश्वम् निहितम् — 'विश्वम्' = सम्पूर्ण जगत्; 'निहितम्' = नि + √धा — 'स्थित / स्थापित' — विश्व ब्रह्म में स्थित, ब्रह्म विश्व में नहीं। भाति शुभ्रम् — 'भाति' = √भा (चमकना) — 'प्रकाशमान'; 'शुभ्रम्' = 'शुद्ध / उज्ज्वल।' उपासते — उप + √आस् (बैठना) — आत्मनेपद बहुवचन — 'उपासना करते हैं / समीप बैठते हैं / ध्यान करते हैं।' पुरुषम् — द्वितीया — कर्म — 'पुरुष को।' अकामाः — अ + काम — बहुव्रीहि — 'काम-रहित / निष्काम' — कामना-यात्रा का चरम: सत्यकाम (3.2.3) → आप्तकाम (3.2.6) → अकाम (3.2.11)। शुक्रम् — √शुच् (शुद्ध होना / चमकना) — 'बीज / तेज / प्रकाशमान सार' — सृष्टि-बीज — जन्म-मरण-चक्र का जनक तत्त्व। अतिवर्तन्ति — अति + √वृत् (घूमना/होना) — 'अतिक्रमण करते हैं / पार कर जाते हैं' — ज्ञानी जन्म-बीज से परे। धीराः — √धी (बुद्धि/ध्यान) — 'धीर / स्थिर-बुद्धि / प्रज्ञावान्' — उपनिषद् का अन्तिम शब्द — सम्पूर्ण शिक्षा का गन्तव्य = 'धीर' — जो ज्ञानी, स्थिर, साहसी — सत्य-अन्वेषी।
Eng: The Muṇḍaka's closing seal. 'Veda' (liṭ of √vid) = knows (with present sense). 'Brahma-dhāma' = brahman + dhāman (√dhā) — abode/glory of Brahman. 'Nihitam' = placed IN Brahman. 'Upāsate' (upa+√ās, ātmanepada plural) = worship/meditate. 'Akāmāḥ' = bahuvrīhi — desireless — the culmination: satya-kāma → āpta-kāma → a-kāma. 'Śukram' = the generative seed/luminous essence. 'Ativartanti' (ati+√vṛt) = transcend. 'Dhīrāḥ' = the Upanishad's final word — the wise, steady, resolute.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — 'परमं ब्रह्मधाम' = निर्गुण ब्रह्म = सर्वाधार (substratum of all)। 'विश्वं निहितम्' = विश्व = ब्रह्म में स्थित — ब्रह्म विश्व में नहीं। 'अकामाः' = निष्काम ज्ञानी — इच्छा-मुक्त। 'शुक्रम् अतिवर्तन्ति' = जन्म-मरण (birth-death cycle) से परे — पुनर्जन्म नहीं — मोक्ष।
advaita.en: Shankara says 'paramaṁ brahma-dhāma' = nirguṇa Brahman = the substratum of all. 'Viśvaṁ nihitam' = the universe rests IN Brahman — not Brahman in the universe. 'Akāmāḥ' = desireless knowers — free from desire. 'Śukram ativartanti' = they go beyond the birth-death cycle — no rebirth — mokṣa.
advaita.ins: The final teaching: the universe rests in Brahman, shining with Brahman's light. The wise — desireless, steady — transcend the very seed of rebirth. They don't go somewhere new. They realise where they've always been — in the supreme abode, where everything shines, where nothing is lacking, where the cycle ends.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — 'परमं ब्रह्मधाम' = भगवान् का दिव्य धाम — वैकुण्ठ — जहाँ विश्व शुभ्र (resplendent) है। 'अकामाः पुरुषं उपासते' = निष्काम भक्त — भगवान् की उपासना — भगवद्-प्रेम (divine love) ही साधन (means) और साध्य (end)। 'शुक्रम् अतिवर्तन्ति' = संसार-चक्र (cycle of rebirth) से मुक्ति — भगवान् के धाम को प्राप्ति।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says 'paramaṁ brahma-dhāma' = the Lord's divine abode — Vaikuṇṭha — where the universe shines resplendent. 'Akāmāḥ puruṣaṁ upāsate' = desireless devotees — worship of God — divine love is both the means and the end. 'Śukram ativartanti' = freedom from the cycle of rebirth — attainment of the Lord's abode.
vishisht.ins: The universe rests in God's supreme abode, shining with His radiance. The desireless devotees who worship Him — they transcend the cycle of birth entirely. Not through knowledge alone, not through action alone — but through love. Love without desire, worship without wanting — that is what takes you beyond.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — 'परमं ब्रह्मधाम' = सच्चिदानन्द (sat-cit-ānanda) — सत्य-चेतना-आनन्द — विश्व का आधार। 'भाति शुभ्रम्' = चेतना = प्रकाशमान (luminous) — जड़ नहीं। 'शुक्रम् अतिवर्तन्ति' = चेतना-विकास (evolution) का शिखर — अतिमानसिक रूपान्तर (supramental transformation) — जन्म-मृत्यु-चक्र से परे।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says 'paramaṁ brahma-dhāma' = sat-cit-ānanda — truth-consciousness-bliss — the ground of the universe. 'Bhāti śubhram' = consciousness = luminous — not inert. 'Śukram ativartanti' = the summit of consciousness-evolution — supramental transformation — beyond the cycle of birth and death.
aurobindo.ins: The universe shines in the supreme abode of consciousness — sat-cit-ānanda. It was never dark, never inert. The wise who worship the Person without desire — they transcend the very seed of becoming. They reach the summit of evolution — where consciousness knows itself fully, and the cycle of birth and death has no more hold.

dp.q: 🔍 The Muṇḍaka's conclusion — 'akāmāḥ' and 'dhīrāḥ'
dp.a:
मुण्डक उपनिषद् दो शब्दों से समाप्त होता है जो सम्पूर्ण शिक्षा का सार हैं: 'अकामाः' (निष्काम) और 'धीराः' (धीर)। 'अकामाः' — कामना-यात्रा की परिपूर्णता: मुण्डक ने कामना की यात्रा तीन चरणों में दिखाई: (1) सत्यकाम (3.2.3): सत्य-प्रेमी — जिनकी कामना सत्य की ओर — प्रस्थान-बिन्दु — कामना अस्वीकृत नहीं, पुनर्दिशित। (2) आप्तकाम (3.2.6): पूर्णकाम — जिन्होंने आत्मा पाया — उसमें सब कामनाएँ तृप्त। (3) अकाम (3.2.11): निष्काम — कामना से पूर्ण अतिक्रमण — दमन नहीं, पूर्णता से — जब स्रोत मिला, शाखाएँ स्वतः गिरीं। क्रम: सत्य-कामना → कामना-तृप्ति → कामनातीत। 'धीराः' — उपनिषद् का अन्तिम शब्द: मुण्डक का अन्तिम शब्द = 'धीराः' — न पण्डित (विद्वान्), न याज्ञिक (कर्मकाण्डी), न तपस्वी — बल्कि 'धीर': बोध में दृढ़, दर्शन में स्थिर, सत्य-अन्वेषण में साहसी। कठ (1.2.1): 'कश्चिद् धीरः प्रत्यगात्मानमैक्षत आवृत्तचक्षुः अमृतत्वमिच्छन्' — 'किसी विरल धीर ने, अमृतत्व चाहकर, दृष्टि भीतर फेरी और आत्मा देखा।' धीर = जो भीतर मुड़ता है।

Eng: The Muṇḍaka Upanishad closes with two key words that summarise its entire teaching: 'Akāmāḥ' (desireless) and 'dhīrāḥ' (the wise/steady): 'Akāmāḥ' — the culmination of the desire-journey: the Muṇḍaka has traced the journey of desire through three stages: (1) Satya-kāma (3.2.3): lovers of truth — those whose desire is directed toward the real. This is the starting point — desire itself is not rejected but redirected. (2) Āpta-kāma (3.2.6): those whose desires are fulfilled — the sages who have found the Self and in it, all desire is satisfied. (3) A-kāma (3.2.11): desireless — those who have transcended desire entirely. Not by suppression but by fulfilment — when the Self is found, no desire remains because the source of all satisfaction is within. The progression is: desire for truth → fulfilment of desire → beyond desire. 'Dhīrāḥ' — the Upanishad's final word: the Muṇḍaka's last word is 'dhīrāḥ' — the wise, the steady, the resolute. This is the Upanishad's ideal: not the intellectual (paṇḍita), not the ritualist (yājñika), not even the ascetic (tapasvin) — but the 'dhīra': one who is firm in understanding, steady in vision, courageous in the pursuit of truth. The Kaṭha (1.2.1) uses the same word: 'parāñci khāni vyatṛṇat svayambhūḥ, tasmāt parāṅ paśyati nāntarātman, kaścid dhīraḥ pratyag-ātmānam aikṣat āvṛtta-cakṣuḥ amṛtatvam icchan' — 'Self-existent [Brahman] pierced the senses outward; therefore one sees outward, not the inner Self. Some rare dhīra, desiring immortality, turned the eyes inward and saw the Self.' The dhīra is the one who turns inward.

dp.q: 🔍 'Śukram ativartanti' — transcending the seed of rebirth
dp.a:
'शुक्रमेतदतिवर्तन्ति' ('वे इस प्रकाशमान बीज को पार कर जाते हैं') — मुण्डक का मुक्ति विषयक अन्तिम वचन। 'शुक्र' क्या है? (1) शाब्दिक: शुक्र = बीज / वीर्य / उज्ज्वल पदार्थ — सृजन-सिद्धान्त — वह सृजनशील बल जो शरीर, जन्म, संसार-निरन्तरता उत्पन्न करता है। (2) प्रतीकात्मक: शुक्र = भव-बीज (becoming-seed) — कर्म-बीज जो भावी जन्मों में अंकुरित — जब तक यह बीज है, जन्म-मरण-चक्र जारी। (3) दार्शनिक: शुक्र = ब्रह्म का वह सृजनात्मक आवेग जो जगत् उत्पन्न करता है — 'तपसा चीयते ब्रह्म, ततोऽन्नमभिजायते' (3.2.1) — शुक्र को पार करके ज्ञानी ब्रह्म के सृजन-कार्य से भी परे। 'अतिवर्तन्ति' का अर्थ: 'पार कर जाते हैं / अतिक्रमण करते हैं' — ज्ञानी संसार से पलायन नहीं करते, वे उस सिद्धान्त को पार करते हैं जो संसार उत्पन्न करता है — जन्म, मृत्यु, भवन, चक्र — सब पार। बृहदारण्यक (4.4.6): 'जब हृदय में छिपी सब कामनाएँ मुक्त हों — तब मर्त्य अमर्त्य — यहीं ब्रह्म-प्राप्ति।' शुक्र (बीज) मुक्त — अन्तिम तन्तु कटा — ज्ञानी भवन-चक्र से मुक्त। यह मुण्डक उपनिषद् का अन्तिम वचन है।

Eng: The phrase 'śukram etat ativartanti' ('they transcend this luminous seed') is the Muṇḍaka's final statement about liberation: What is 'śukra'? (1) Literally: śukra = seed / semen / bright substance. It represents the generative principle — the creative force that produces bodies, births, and the continuity of saṁsāra. (2) Symbolically: śukra = the seed of becoming (bhava-bīja) — the karmic seed that germinates into future births. As long as this seed exists, the cycle of birth and death continues. (3) Philosophically: śukra = the creative impulse of Brahman that produces the world — 'tapasā cīyate brahma, tataḥ annam abhijāyate' (3.2.1). By transcending the śukra, the wise go beyond even Brahman's creative function. What does 'ativartanti' mean? 'Ativartanti' = they 'pass beyond' / 'transcend' / 'go beyond.' The wise don't merely escape the world — they transcend the very principle that generates worlds. They go beyond birth, beyond death, beyond becoming, beyond the cycle itself. The Bṛhadāraṇyaka parallel (4.4.6): 'When all the desires that lurk in the heart are released, then the mortal becomes immortal — here he attains Brahman.' The 'śukra' (seed) is released, and with it, the last thread connecting the sage to the cycle of becoming is cut. The Muṇḍaka concludes: the wise — desireless, steady, knowers of the supreme abode — transcend the seed of rebirth and are free. This is the final word of the Muṇḍaka Upanishad.
